title: Don't Try to Out-Hawk the Hawks: Progressive ForPol Advisor Matt Duss on Democrats, Détente, and 2028
summary_zh: 2026年美国中期选举民主党重掌国会两院之际，Kaiser Kuo与联合主持Samm Sacks对话进步派外交顾问、Bernie Sanders前幕僚Matt Duss，探讨美国左翼的对华定位、特朗普第二任期的对华缓和及2028年政策走向。三人坦言，尽管动机迥异，特朗普在稀土反制与市场考量下的对华缓和客观上降低了冲突风险。Matt Duss剖析了民主党内战略竞争派、克制派与反垄断派的分野，反对以“中国威胁”作为一切外交与产业政策的借口，主张借鉴“国家约束资本”的思路监管Nvidia与Anthropic等科技寡头，并在台海维持低烈度现状。展望2028年，他警示民主党切勿与右翼比拼对华鹰派姿态，而应认清真正的对手是导致美国去工业化与金钱政治的本土大企业及权贵精英。
key_takeaways_zh: 美国外交政策应回归保障本国安全与繁荣的本源，切忌重蹈“反恐战争”覆辙，将“对华竞争”异化为统摄一切议题的单一滤镜与合理化借口。
后新自由主义时代的核心启示在于逆转“华盛顿共识”，从“资本约束国家”转向“国家约束资本”，中国在严管科技行业的同时实现技术突围便是明证。
民主党内部目前分裂为维护霸权的“战略竞争派”、反战的“克制派”与反对权力集中的“反垄断派”，尚未形成稳固的对华共识，且试图靠渲染外部敌意来重建美国国内政治共识注定徒劳。
硅谷科技寡头以“输掉对华AI竞赛”为由抗拒监管的叙事已难获民意认同，美国推进基础设施建设与产业政策完全可以立足民生需求，无需动辄打“中国牌”。
民主党在2028年大选中绝不应与共和党比拼对华鹰派姿态，而应将民众的不满精准指向掏空美国制造业、操弄合法化贿赂的本土跨国企业与寡头精英。

highlights.title_zh: 与特朗普意外趋同的荒诞感
highlights.summary_zh: Kaiser Kuo与Samm Sacks坦言，在特朗普开启第二任期两年后，长期批评华盛顿对华鹰派共识的他们，在对华议题上竟发现自己比起建制派反对者更接近特朗普的立场。Samm指出，当前华盛顿舆论氛围高度敏感，即便肯定美国领导人从“共存”与“承认多极化”出发处理对华关系，也往往迫使研究者自我审查。
highlights.quote_en: On China, and on just this one thing I suspect, I find myself much closer to the president than to most of the people lining up against him.

highlights.title_zh: 进步派困境与美中缓和空间
highlights.summary_zh: 针对进步派在气候合作与劳工权益之间的对华认知张力，Matt Duss指出，特朗普第二任期加征关税遭遇中国稀土反制后，美中反而进入了值得肯定的“缓和”（détente）阶段。他强调，美国绝不应重蹈过去二十五年以反恐统摄一切的覆辙，而应以本国安全与繁荣为出发点来定义对华关系，拒绝将“对华竞争”当作所有外交政策的单一滤镜。
highlights.quote_en: Now we're in this moment of essentially détente. And I think that's good.

highlights.title_zh: 逆转华盛顿共识：国家约束资本
highlights.summary_zh: 谈及如何界定中国体制，Matt Duss引述Bernie Sanders的评价称中国实为“受控的资本主义”，其对后新自由主义时代最大的启示在于敢于“约束资本”。他指出，“华盛顿共识”曾信奉由资本约束国家，而如今美国亟需逆转这一逻辑；中国在严密监管科技等行业的同时仍取得显著技术突破，证明政府监管与技术创新并非对立。
highlights.quote_en: The basic bargain of neoliberalism is that states must be disciplined by capital. And we realize now that it's the reverse: states have to discipline capital in various ways.

highlights.title_zh: 民主党对华立场的三派分野
highlights.summary_zh: Matt Duss将民主党内的对华主张划分为三大阵营：以Jake Sullivan为代表、试图借“中国威胁”维系美国霸权并重塑国内政治共识的“战略竞争派”，主张外交收缩的“克制派”，以及警惕跨国供应链与寡头垄断的“反垄断派”。他援引Bernie Sanders的文章警告，民主与威权的真正较量发生在一国国内而非国家之间，靠煽动对单一国家的敌意无法重建持久的国内共识。
highlights.quote_en: The struggle between democracy and authoritarianism is not primarily happening between states; it's happening within states, including ours.

highlights.title_zh: 破除新冷战迷思与青年转向
highlights.summary_zh: 回顾Bernie Sanders的对华立场轨迹，Matt Duss指出其早年反对给予中国永久正常贸易关系（PNTR）源于对新自由主义全球化神话的怀疑，而如今他同样拒绝接受“美中注定走向新冷战”的新建制派教条。与此同时，受DeepSeek问世、“TikTok难民”涌入小红书及公众厌战情绪推动，美国Z世代对华态度显著改观，民调显示民众并不寻求对华冲突。
highlights.quote_en: Yeah, I was calling BS on the old consensus, and now I'm calling BS on what looks to be a quickly forming new consensus.

highlights.title_zh: 科技寡头博弈与金钱政治病灶
highlights.summary_zh: 围绕Jensen Huang复职Nvidia引发的风波及Anthropic渲染“中国生存威胁”的游说策略，Matt Duss批评硅谷借“赢下AI竞赛”逃避政府监管的荒谬话术，指出特朗普看重AI巨头纯粹是为维系股市泡沫。他进一步剖析称，特朗普家族赤裸裸的利益输送并非孤立现象，而是将美国长期存在的竞选献金“合法化贿赂”与寡头干政从潜台词直接搬上了台面。
highlights.quote_en: Donald Trump's talent is kind of turning the subtext into text.

highlights.title_zh: 拒打中国牌与2028竞选戒律
highlights.summary_zh: 展望2027年新一届国会与2028年大选，Matt Duss警告民主党切勿重犯从右翼攻击共和党外交政策的旧病，因为民主党永远不可能在民族主义竞价中胜过右翼。在产业政策上，他呼吁政客戒除动辄打“中国牌”的政治懒政，坦诚地以改善本土基建与民生福祉本身来争取选民支持。
highlights.quote_en: You will never out-nationalist the right. I mean, they will always like raise you.

highlights.title_zh: 台海政策：维持现状与降温
highlights.summary_zh: 针对AOC在慕尼黑安全会议上就台湾问题停顿数秒引发的争议，当时在场的Matt Duss为其辩护称，面对潜在全球冲突理应审慎作答，且她给出“避免走到军事冲突那一步”的答案完全正确。他结合访问台北时与当地进步派人士的交流指出，当前维持一个中国政策与“虽不完美但最稳妥的现状”、以非挑衅方式协助台湾自卫并保持局势降温，才是最务实的路径。
highlights.quote_en: From my view, this deeply unsatisfying status quo is probably the best we've got.

highlights.title_zh: 民主党的清算：选对真正敌人
highlights.summary_zh: 面对前拜登政府国安鹰派与反战、反垄断民意之间的路线冲突，Matt Duss指出民主党破局的关键在于“选对敌人”。他强调，当年掏空美国铁锈地带、将就业岗位外迁的并非中国，而是受腐败政客税收优惠纵容的美国跨国企业；唯有将矛头直指本土大企业与自肥的权贵寡头，才能真正瓦解反华恐慌叙事。
highlights.quote_en: The way we're going to kind of suppress and beat the anti-China argument is by choosing the right enemy. The right enemy is corporate America.

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Absolutely. It's a moment where, coming out of the midterms, we're in a new reality, right? And come January, the Democrats are going to be in firm control of both houses of Congress.
transcript.zh: 完全如此。随着中期选举落幕，我们已经置身于一种新的现实之中，对吧？到了明年一月，民主党将牢牢掌控国会参众两院。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: And I think the Democrats have a reckoning ahead of them. So I am really eager to explore with all of you what lies ahead for the next two years, for the remainder of Trump's presidency, and what are we looking at after that.
transcript.zh: 我认为民主党正面临一场深刻的清算与反思。因此我非常期待与大家一同探讨，在特朗普任期余下的这两年里将会发生什么，以及那之后又将呈现怎样的局面。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah. So, fortunately, with us to talk about all this is somebody who's been thinking hard about what a different American foreign policy might look like, and who, you know, has the ear of some of the people who may one day be in a position to really carry it out.
transcript.zh: 没错。幸运的是，今天与我们一同探讨这些问题的嘉宾，长期以来一直在深入思考另一种美国外交政策可能会是什么模样，而且他的意见能够直达那些未来有朝一日或许真正掌握执行权的人。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Matt Duss is executive vice president of the Center for International Policy in Washington. From 2017 to 2022, he was foreign policy advisor to Senator Bernie Sanders, and he served as foreign policy director on the Sanders presidential campaign in 2020.
transcript.zh: Matt Duss现任华盛顿国际政策中心执行副总裁。2017年至2022年间，他曾担任参议员Bernie Sanders的外交政策顾问，并在2020年Sanders总统竞选团队中担任外交政策主管。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Before the Sanders years, he ran the Foundation for Middle East Peace, and he's also spent time at the Center for American Progress and the Carnegie Endowment. These days, he advises a number of progressive members of Congress, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez among them.
transcript.zh: 在加入Sanders团队之前，他曾执掌中东和平基金会，并先后在美国进步中心和卡内基国际和平研究院任职。如今，他为多位进步派国会议员提供咨询，其中包括Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Earlier this year, he edited a volume of essays called A World for All, with a foreword by Senator Sanders, that tries to set out what a progressive foreign policy would look like.
transcript.zh: 今年早些时候，他主编了一本文集《A World for All》，由参议员Sanders作序，试图勾勒出进步派外交政策的蓝图。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And just days after the midterms, he published a piece in Foreign Affairs calling on the new Congress to deliver a true foreign policy revolution. It's a piece about ending the war in Iran, about corruption, and about the cost of living. It's not a piece about China.
transcript.zh: 就在中期选举结束几天后，他在《外交事务》发表文章，呼吁新一届国会掀起一场真正的外交政策革命。那篇文章谈的是结束对伊朗的战争、反腐败以及生活成本问题，并没有谈及中国。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So Samm and I thought we'd ask him about China. Matt Duss, welcome to Sinica.
transcript.zh: 于是Samm和我决定借此机会向他请教中国议题。Matt Duss，欢迎来到Sinica。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Thanks so much for having me.
transcript.zh: 非常感谢你们的邀请。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Good to be with you both.
transcript.zh: 很高兴能与两位对话。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And I guess things, you know, are moving very fast. We should probably timestamp this one. It's the morning of Wednesday, November 25th here in Beijing, evening of November 24th there in the US, on the East Coast, as we tape.
transcript.zh: 眼下局势变化很快，我们或许应该先标注一下录制时间。现在是北京时间11月25日周三上午，美国东海岸则是11月24日傍晚。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: We are about, I guess what, like 36 hours after the news broke that Jensen Huang had been reinstated, a week past the trilateral meeting in Shenzhen at APEC. So we're really still in the middle of what our friend Graham Webster has aptly described as a hyperspectacle.
transcript.zh: 距离黄仁勋复职的消息传出大约过去了36个小时，距离深圳APEC三方会晤也已过去一周。因此我们依然身处我们的朋友Graham Webster精准形容的所谓“超奇观”（hyperspectacle）之中。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Oh, and happy Thanksgiving, guys.
transcript.zh: 对了，祝两位感恩节快乐。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah, thank you. Happy Thanksgiving.
transcript.zh: 谢谢，也祝你感恩节快乐。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: All right, well. Matt, I wanted to start out with what I call the progressives' China problem. It's been interesting watching how progressives have tried to figure out where they are when it comes to China.
transcript.zh: 好的。Matt，我想先从我所谓的“进步派的中国难题”聊起。观察进步派如何试图在中国议题上找准自身立场，一直是一件很有意思的事。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: On one side of the ledger, you have China's contribution to the green energy transition, made possible really by the disciplining of capital under state capitalism.
transcript.zh: 从账本的正面来看，中国为绿色能源转型作出了贡献，而这在很大程度上得益于国家资本主义体制下对资本的规训。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You have China's anti-imperialist standing, its support for the so-called Axis of Resistance, its restraint thus far from waging wars of its own.
transcript.zh: 此外，还有中国的反帝国主义立场、对所谓“抵抗轴心”的支持，以及迄今为止在避免亲自发动战争方面所展现的克制。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: But there's also, of course, the other side of the ledger: no independent trade unions, something that matters for people who care about the working class, financial repression, and of course its own conduct toward its smaller neighbors and toward its own ethnic minorities.
transcript.zh: 但账本的另一面同样存在：没有独立工会——这对关心工人阶级的人来说至关重要——还有金融抑制，以及中国对待周边较小邻国和本国少数民族的做法。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And then, of course, there's how China impacts our own domestic politics, where, on issues from tariffs and EVs, sometimes it's like it's the climate left against the labor left.
transcript.zh: 当然，还有中国对美国国内政治的影响——在关税、电动车等议题上，有时甚至演变成气候左翼与劳工左翼之间的对立。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So Matt, how do you try to hold both? I mean, do you nudge progressives toward one side or the other? What's your approach on this?
transcript.zh: 那么Matt，你是如何试着兼顾这两方面的？你会引导进步派偏向其中某一方吗？你在这个问题上是什么思路？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah, well, thank you. And you know, I was listening to your intro here.
transcript.zh: 好的，谢谢。听着你刚才的开场白，我很有感触。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And we're in a moment right now where we have a President Donald Trump who, in his first term, really shifted the American foreign policy paradigm toward competition with China and made China the key focus of American foreign policy.
transcript.zh: 我们正处在这样一个时刻：现任总统特朗普在他的第一个任期内，真正将美国外交政策范式转向了与中国竞争，并把中国变成了美国外交政策的核心焦点。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: That first National Security Strategy in the first Trump administration—for all the efforts that the previous administration, Barack Obama, had made to pivot to Asia, you know, Trump seemed really prepared to do it.
transcript.zh: 看特朗普第一任期的首份《国家安全战略》就能发现，尽管前任奥巴马政府曾大力推动“重返亚太”，但特朗普似乎才真正下定决心要这么做。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And then the Biden administration really picked up the ball from them. They made China—again, strategic competition was the name of the game. China became the lens through which all of US foreign policy was focused; it became the justification for everything.
transcript.zh: 随后拜登政府实际上接过了这一棒。再一次地，“战略竞争”成了主旋律。中国成了审视所有美国外交政策的棱镜，也成了一切政策举措的正当化理由。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And then Donald Trump was reelected, and things happened. He declared Liberation Day, tariffs on everyone.
transcript.zh: 后来特朗普再次当选，一系列事情接踵而至。他宣布了“解放日”，对所有国家加征关税。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: China made clear that it had cards to play, specifically on rare earth minerals, and Donald Trump was like, "Oh crap, I didn't really think about that."
transcript.zh: 中国则明确表明自己手中有牌可打，特别是在稀土矿产方面，结果特朗普的反应就像：“糟了，我之前还真没考虑到这一点。”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But now we're in this moment of essentially détente. And I think that's good.
transcript.zh: 但现在，我们进入了一个实质上的缓和期。我认为这是件好事。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right.
transcript.zh: 没错。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah, not being a huge booster of Donald Trump, but like, if you had asked me a few years ago, where will things be between the US and China in November 2026, I would not have predicted they would be where they are.
transcript.zh: 是的，我绝非特朗普的狂热支持者，但如果你几年前问我，2026年11月的美中关系会处于什么状态，我绝对预测不到会像现在这样。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So, I mean, I'm also someone who has said, and I think people should support Trump when he does good things.
transcript.zh: 所以我一直认为，当特朗普做出正确的事情时，大家也应该予以支持。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Like, for example, early in his administration, it did seem like he was prepared to actually do diplomacy with Iran, to get to some kind of agreement around their nuclear program.
transcript.zh: 举个例子，在他本届任期伊始，他确实一度看起来准备真正同伊朗开展外交，围绕其核计划达成某种协议。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Of course he changed that. He launched the first—the war last June, and this ridiculous war since February that we're still stuck in this stalemate now.
transcript.zh: 当然，他后来改变了主意。他在去年6月发动了第一场战争，又从今年2月起陷入了这场荒谬的战争，至今我们仍深陷僵局之中。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But if the president, whoever that president is, is willing to do good things, I think we should acknowledge it.
transcript.zh: 但无论谁担任总统，只要他愿意做正确的事情，我认为我们就应当予以肯定。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And having this détente with China such that it seems that there is space to talk through the multitude of issues that the US and China have to talk through, to reach some, if we can, kind of coexistence.
transcript.zh: 与中国保持这种缓和状态，使得美中双方似乎有了空间去逐一磋商那些亟待解决的诸多议题，并在可能的情况下达成某种共存。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean, the two biggest, most important economies in the world—we really have to try at least to find a way to work together. So I just wanted to get that said.
transcript.zh: 毕竟作为世界上最大、最重要的两个经济体，我们至少必须努力找到合作共处之道。我只是想先把这一点说明白。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Amen.
transcript.zh: 说得太对了。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Even though Donald Trump—it's not like he has a plan. Who knows the mind of Donald J. Trump and why he makes these decisions?
transcript.zh: 尽管特朗普并非真有什么全盘规划。谁能摸透特朗普的心思，知道他为什么会做出这些决定呢？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: As best I can tell, he's always thinking about, "Okay, what can I do that just kind of makes Donald Trump look awesome?"
transcript.zh: 据我观察，他脑子里想的永远是：“好吧，我做什么才能让特朗普看起来威风八面？”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But still, this relationship is not as hot and not heading headlong toward a conflict scenario as I might have feared, as I actually did fear just a few years ago.
transcript.zh: 但无论如何，目前这段关系不再那么剑拔弩张，也没有像我几年前所担心的——或者说当时确实感到恐惧的那样——一头扎向冲突情景。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So the question is, okay, what do we do with that? Where do Democrats land?
transcript.zh: 所以问题在于：接下来我们该怎么应对这种局面？民主党又该站在什么立场上？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And as you said, in the book that I edited that came out just a few weeks ago—actually on Election Day, not to make things too on the nose—there's a great chapter on US and China by Jake Werner, who's head of the East Asia program at the Quincy Institute, and San—
transcript.zh: 正如你提到的，我主编的新书几周前刚出版——巧合的是就在大选日当天出版，倒像是刻意安排的一样——其中有一篇关于美中关系的精彩章节，由昆西研究所东亚项目主任Jake Werner和San——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: ...dy Shan, who's the director of Justice Is Global, that really looks at these issues, and they really are the experts.
transcript.zh: ……也就是Justice Is Global主任Sandy Shan，她深入研究过这些问题，他们才是真正的专家。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: My own training is not in China or Asia, but I'm looking at this in the broader scope of what relationship we need between the United States and China to advance American security and prosperity.
transcript.zh: 我本人的学术背景并非中国或亚洲研究，但我是在一个更宏大的框架下审视这个问题：我们需要怎样的美中关系，才能促进美国的安全与繁荣？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And I guess that's where I might land this: so much of Washington is still all about how the US needs to compete with China.
transcript.zh: 我想我的落脚点就在这里：华盛顿的很多人至今仍满脑子想着“美国必须与中国竞争”。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I start from the premise that the goal of US foreign policy is to promote American security and prosperity. What does a relationship with China look like that does those things?
transcript.zh: 而我的出发点是：美国外交政策的目标是促进美国的安全与繁荣。能够实现这些目标的对华关系应该是什么样的？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Because my problem with the—
transcript.zh: 因为我认为问题在于——

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: A good starting place.
transcript.zh: 这是个很好的出发点。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: That's the starting place, you know. I don't want to define all of our foreign policy through the China lens.
transcript.zh: 这就是出发点。我不想把我们所有的外交政策都放在“中国视角”下来定义。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yes, it's an important relationship—it's among the most important relationships the US has—but we have just come out of 25 years where the United States defined its entire foreign policy through the lens of counterterrorism and Islamic extremism, and that was very stupid.
transcript.zh: 没错，这是一段重要的关系，是美国最重要的双边关系之一。但我们刚刚走过25年——在这25年里，美国完全通过反恐和伊斯兰极端主义的棱镜来定义整个外交政策，这非常愚蠢。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: It was essentially giving an adversary or a set of adversaries control over the way we defined our foreign policy. I think we need to define our needs and our goals ourselves, and then think about what relationship with China serves those goals.
transcript.zh: 这实质上是把我们定义自身外交政策的主导权交给了某个或某几个对手。我认为我们需要自己界定我们的需求和目标，然后再去思考：怎样的对华关系才能服务于这些目标？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, I feel like the progressives don't even know exactly what to call China's system. You see a lot of debates over whether China is in fact a socialist state or whether it's just sort of the apotheosis of neoliberalism.
transcript.zh: 我觉得进步派甚至都不知道到底该怎么称呼中国的体制。你能看到很多争论：中国究竟是一个社会主义国家，还是新自由主义的极致体现？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Is it state capitalism, you know? And what is it for you, or for Bernie, or for AOC? I mean, what do you guys refer to China as?
transcript.zh: 还是说它是国家资本主义？对你而言，或者对Bernie、对AOC而言，你们怎么界定中国？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Well, no, it's funny. I actually had this conversation with Bernie. He would remark that they were far more capitalist than he was, when he would talk with Chinese analysts—
transcript.zh: 这很有意思。我其实跟Bernie讨论过这个问题。他常感慨说，当他跟中国分析人士交流时，发现他们比他自己要资本主义得多——

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: That's not hard.
transcript.zh: 这倒也不难做到。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah, it's not hard. Okay, sure. But exactly: they call themselves the Chinese Communist Party, but it is a kind of controlled capitalism.
transcript.zh: 是啊，确实不难。不过说到底，他们自称中国共产党，但实行的是一种受控的资本主义。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: They do a lot of things that I think a lot of capitalists here would love to do, as you said: suppress trade unions, suppress other kinds of freedoms.
transcript.zh: 正如你所说，他们做了很多美国这边的资本家梦寐以求的事：压制工会，压制其他各类自由。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But at the same time—and you put it so well, it's a term I've also used—they are not shy about disciplining capital. And that is what we need to be doing here.
transcript.zh: 但与此同时——你概括得非常精准，这也是我一直使用的说法——他们毫不忌讳“规训资本”。而这正是我们美国需要做的事情。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And I do think that is one of the most important insights in the post-neoliberal shift that we're seeing. That was the memo that landed in 2016 with the election of Donald Trump.
transcript.zh: 我认为，这是我们当前看到的“后新自由主义转向”中最重要的洞见之一。2016年特朗普当选，实际上就宣告了这一现实。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: This whole Washington Consensus about how the key to prosperity and freedom is just to free capital from any constraints—the basic bargain of neoliberalism is that states must be disciplined by capital.
transcript.zh: 整套“华盛顿共识”认为繁荣与自由的关键就是让资本摆脱一切束缚，而新自由主义的底层契约就是国家必须受资本规训。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And we realize now that it's the reverse: states have to discipline capital in various ways. China certainly has been doing that, and I think we should do that.
transcript.zh: 而我们现在意识到事实恰恰相反：国家必须以各种方式去规训资本。中国显然一直在这么做，我认为我们也应该这么做。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Now, the way we do that will not look like the way China is doing that; I think we have a set of other priorities.
transcript.zh: 当然，我们这么做的方式不会和中国完全一样，我认为我们有自己不同的优先事项。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But still, with Samm having worked on the tech issues here—I don't want to jump too far ahead—we're having this weird debate about whether we set free our tech champions or regulate them.
transcript.zh: 不过话说回来，Samm一直研究这里的科技议题——我不想扯得太远——但我们现在正陷入一场奇怪的争论：我们究竟该给自己的科技龙头企业松绑，还是该加强监管？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And for me, the answer is: listen, China heavily regulates its tech industry, all its industries, and yet it has managed pretty significant technological advances.
transcript.zh: 对我而言，答案很明确：你看，中国对科技行业乃至所有行业都实施了严格监管，但即便如此，它依然取得了相当可观的技术进步。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So I think there's things we can learn from that, but still, the imperatives of the old neoliberal order are hard to break. I mean, the establishment remains the establishment.
transcript.zh: 所以我认为这其中有很多值得我们借鉴的地方。不过，旧的新自由主义秩序的惯性依然难以打破，建制派终究还是建制派。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Matt, on this point that they are more capitalist than Bernie, it begs the question: progressives love the word solidarity, so when it comes to China, what does that mean?
transcript.zh: Matt，顺着你刚才说的“他们比Bernie还要资本主义”这一点，这就引出了一个问题：进步派非常喜欢用“团结”这个词，那么放到中国问题上，它究竟意味着什么？

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Solidarity with whom? What does worker solidarity mean, to your point, when there are no independent unions? And more: who do we partner with?
transcript.zh: 和谁团结？正如你刚才指出的，在没有独立工会的背景下，“工人团结”意味着什么？更进一步说，我们又能与谁合作？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah. No, I mean, that's a great question. First of all, even if it's not trade unions, I think the United States should press the issue of allowing people to organize, whether in China or anywhere.
transcript.zh: 嗯，这是一个非常好的问题。首先，哪怕不是传统意义上的工会，我也认为美国应该敦促允许民众自主组织起来——无论是在中国还是其他任何地方。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I think that is a right people should have. We should also be—especially after the experience of the past 25 years in the Middle East—modest about the United States' ability to transform societies.
transcript.zh: 我认为这是人们理应享有的权利。同时，尤其是在经历了过去25年中东的教训之后，我们对美国改造他国社会的能力应当保持谦卑。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But it is something I think we should raise. I think that does matter.
transcript.zh: 但这个问题我依然认为我们应该提出来，我认为这确实很重要。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But I also think we should just be in solidarity with the people of China.
transcript.zh: 不过我也认为，我们理应与中国人民站在一起。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: These are people who are just seeking a—
transcript.zh: 他们只是在寻求一种——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: decent life, a life of prosperity and safety, a good future for their children. I think there is a basis there for an understanding between our two countries.
transcript.zh: 体面的生活，过上繁荣安稳的日子，让孩子拥有美好的未来。我认为，这为我们两国达成相互理解奠定了基础。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: You know, the Chinese government, the Chinese Communist Party, may have a vision for its role in the world and the way that global affairs are ordered that is not consonant with mine or many progressives.
transcript.zh: 诚然，中国政府和中国共产党对于自身在世界上的角色以及全球事务的秩序安排，或许有着与我或许多进步派不同的愿景。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But I think starting from the basis of, you know, the American people and the people of China—American workers and Chinese workers—need not be in a kind of zero-sum competition for resources and prosperity.
transcript.zh: 但我认为，从根本上说，美国人民与中国人民、美国工人与中国工人，并不需要为了资源与繁荣陷入某种零和博弈。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And I think this is again going back to my book, like, I think we should start from the approach of let's not do harm.
transcript.zh: 再回到我的书里谈到的观点，我认为我们应当秉持“不造成伤害”的出发点。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Let's not promote our own security by promoting insecurity onto others. Let's not promote our prosperity by exporting poverty onto others.
transcript.zh: 不要通过向他国输出不安全来增进自身安全，也不要通过向他国输出贫困来增进自身繁荣。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Let's understand that our security and prosperity is bound up with communities around the world. That's the way we get to a safer world and a safer America, and that includes the people of China.
transcript.zh: 我们应当认识到，美国自身的安全与繁荣同世界各地的社群息息相关。只有这样，才能实现一个更安全的世界和更安全的美国，而这也包括中国人民在内。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, while we're on the subject of class and of, you know, this idea of exporting poverty, I don't know if you've read Klein and Pettis's Trade Wars Are Class Wars.
transcript.zh: 既然谈到阶级问题和“输出贫困”这个概念，不知你是否读过 Klein 和 Pettis 合著的《贸易战就是阶级战》（Trade Wars Are Class Wars）。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You know, it's this book that criticizes Chinese policy—financial repression, underconsumption, overcapacity, and all that stuff. And it goes after China's model on ostensibly pro-worker grounds, but basically because—do you have a take on that?
transcript.zh: 这本书批评中国的政策，涉及金融抑制、消费不足、产能过剩等等。它表面上打着维护工人利益的旗号抨击中国模式，但实质上——你对此有什么看法？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah, no, I mean, listen, I've been a part of a number of conversations with colleagues in labor unions here in the United States, and I recognize that.
transcript.zh: 是的，我参加过不少与美国工会同行的交流，我确实能感受到这种观点。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: First, labor unions coming from a protectionist place—they believe that US policy should protect American workers. And I get that American foreign policy should work on behalf of the American people. It should prioritize the needs of American workers.
transcript.zh: 首先，工会是从保护主义的立场出发，认为美国政策应当保护美国工人。我也理解，美国外交政策理应代表美国人民的利益，理应优先考虑美国工人的需求。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I get that. So there are going to be steps that are entirely appropriate that some neoliberals will call protectionist, that I have no problem whatsoever. I'm not opposed to tariffs.
transcript.zh: 这一点我完全理解。因此，有些完全合理的举措会被新自由主义者贴上“保护主义”的标签，但我对此毫无异议，我也并不反对关税。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I think the fact that we've broken the taboo on tariffs is actually positive. I don't agree with the way that Donald Trump has used them. He just kind of throws them around as a form of punishment—
transcript.zh: 我认为打破对关税的禁忌其实是件好事。不过我并不认同特朗普使用关税的方式。他只是随意挥舞关税大棒，将其当作一种惩罚手段——

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Spray and pray.
transcript.zh: “漫天扫射，听天由命”。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah, exactly—as a way to just extract tribute. He uses them essentially as a form of sanction.
transcript.zh: 对，正是如此——借此索取贡赋。他本质上是把关税当成制裁手段来用。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But I'm very glad that we have broken from the old religious taboo on sanction as this kind of market-distorting, unacceptable thing, as if there is some kind of form of perfect market free from any outside influence, which has always been false.
transcript.zh: 但我很高兴我们打破了过去那种教条式的禁忌——过去总是把制裁视为某种扭曲市场、不可接受的做法，仿佛真的存在一个不受任何外部影响的完美市场一样，而这种假设从来都是虚假的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah.
transcript.zh: 没错。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Let's pivot and talk about human rights, because I think this is something that for someone skeptical of broad sanctions, as many people on the left are, what are the tools to address human rights concerns?
transcript.zh: 我们换个话题，聊聊人权问题。对于像许多左翼人士那样对全面制裁持怀疑态度的人来说，有哪些工具可以用来应对人权关切呢？

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Because we can't ignore that in thinking about navigating this relationship.
transcript.zh: 因为我们在思考如何处理美中关系时，不可能回避这个问题。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah, absolutely. First off—and this is not a kind of sequential thing, I think these are things that have to happen in parallel—first, I think the United States does need to look to its own house.
transcript.zh: 当然。首先——而且这并不是分先后顺序的事，我认为这些工作必须齐头并进——首先，美国确实需要反躬自省，清理好自己的门户。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: You know, we really need to look to some of the methods we've been using internally, not just over the past few years, but going back a long time—police abuse—
transcript.zh: 我们必须正视自己国内长期以来采取的一些做法，不只是过去几年，而是由来已久的问题——比如警察滥权——

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, for me that is sequential. That does come first.
transcript.zh: 对我来说这倒是有先后顺序的。这确实应该排在第一位。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Well, no, and again, I'm not saying we need to solve our own problems at home before we speak out about human rights internationally. But I do think our ability to advance the idea of universal human rights—which is part of our political identity in the United States.
transcript.zh: 倒也不是说我们必须先解决好国内的所有问题，才能在国际上就人权问题发声。不过，至于我们推动普世人权理念的能力——毕竟人权也是美国政治认同的一部分。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: It's literally written into our Declaration of Independence, the idea that all people are created equal and are endowed with inalienable rights. That means a lot to me. I think it means a lot to most Americans.
transcript.zh: 它就实实在在地写在美国《独立宣言》之中，即人人生而平等，并被赋予不可剥夺的权利。这对我意义重大，我想对大多数美国人也是如此。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But then we get to the question of, like, okay, what tools and what right do we have to actually try and promote that, let alone impose it on other countries?
transcript.zh: 但接下来就会面临一个问题：我们究竟拥有什么工具、又有什么权利去努力推广这些理念，更不用说将其强加给其他国家了？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And I would say what we need to do is actually work through the international system, work through the UN to try and uphold a shared set of human rights values.
transcript.zh: 我认为我们应当做的，是切实通过国际体系、通过联合国来努力维护一套共同的人权价值观。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And yes, when countries, including China, are violating those—as China is pretty egregiously in a number of instances—to marshal an international consensus to put pressure on that government to change its behavior.
transcript.zh: 而且，当包括中国在内的某些国家践踏这些价值时——正如中国在不少事件中表现得相当恶劣那样——我们就应当凝聚国际共识，向有关政府施压，促使其改变行为。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Matt, have you ever attempted—let's call it a taxonomy of left positions in the US on China? I mean, I wonder how you'd categorize them.
transcript.zh: Matt，你有没有试着对美国左翼在对华问题上的各种立场做过一种“分类学”梳理？我想知道你会怎么归类。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, I suppose you got your restrainers, you know, people affiliated with Quincy—
transcript.zh: 我是说，我想这其中有主张克制的“克制派”，也就是与昆西研究所（Quincy）相关的人士——

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: There are both on both sides of the fence, but on the left, certainly a lot of restrainers. You have the sort of labor protectionist wing, the human rights left—we were just talking about that issue—the climate left.
transcript.zh: 两边阵营都有这类人，但左翼中确实有很多克制派。此外还有劳工保护主义派、人权左翼——我们刚才正聊到这个议题——以及气候左翼。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And I suppose you have campists. I don't know if that word is still used, but it means, you know, leftists who are basically going to support any country or any organization that opposes the US and the West.
transcript.zh: 我想还有“阵营主义者”（campists）。我不知道这个词现在是否还在用，但它的意思就是指那些基本上只要是反对美国和西方的国家或组织都会支持的左翼人士。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So where are the real groupings? Where are the real fights?
transcript.zh: 那么，真正的派别划分在哪里？真正的争论焦点又在哪里？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Well, as I see it right now, the most interesting discussion happening, at least in the Democratic Party—and we can talk more broadly, too, the Republican Party and others.
transcript.zh: 嗯，依我目前的观察，最有意思的讨论至少正在民主党内部展开——当然我们也可以更宽泛地聊聊共和党和其他群体。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, I'm talking about the Democrats.
transcript.zh: 对，我说的就是民主党。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Okay, so you've got—well, I would say there are three camps. You've got, again, the strategic competition camp, which is, you know, this is what we saw from the Biden administration. I think Jake Sullivan's speech at the Brookings Institution in April 2023 really laid this out.
transcript.zh: 好，那其实可以说有三大阵营。首先还是“战略竞争派”，也就是我们在拜登政府时期看到的那套做法。我认为 Jake Sullivan 2023年4月在布鲁金斯学会的演讲，就把这套逻辑讲得非常透彻了。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So it's a break from the neoliberal model, but it's also—it supports, you know, government intervention in the market to shape markets, but it's also basically about sustaining American primacy, right?
transcript.zh: 所以它既是对新自由主义模式的决裂——也就是支持政府干预市场、塑造市场——但归根结底，它仍然是为了维持美国的主导地位，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Ultimately, it's recognizing, okay, the old neoliberal model did not help American workers, the costs were huge, and the prosperity, while it was real, was not spread around remotely equally.
transcript.zh: 说到底，这套思路承认：旧的新自由主义模式并没有惠及美国工人，代价极其高昂；虽然它确实创造了繁荣，但分配远远谈不上均等。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: It accrued to a very small elite, and it had a lot of negative consequences. It has actually driven a lot of populism, including right-wing populism.
transcript.zh: 财富只流向了极少数精英，并带来了一连串负面后果。事实上，这正是民粹主义——包括右翼民粹主义——大量滋生的重要推手。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And again, this is not new. This is, you know, the insight going back to John Maynard Keynes or even farther, just like inequality promotes essentially fascism. And that's part of what we're facing.
transcript.zh: 再说一遍，这并不新鲜。这个洞见可以追溯到 John Maynard Keynes 甚至更早时期——简而言之，不平等从本质上会助长法西斯主义。而这正是我们眼下面临的部分现实。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: You know, and China has faced its own version of this, but leaving that aside. So you've got essentially the Washington establishment that, you know, yes, we're going to break more or less from neoliberalism, but we're going to use this new China threat—
transcript.zh: 当然，中国也面临着属于自己的这类问题，不过这个话题我们暂且搁置。于是你会看到，华盛顿建制派基本上就是这样一种态度：没错，我们要在某种程度上告别新自由主义，但我们要拿这个新的“中国威胁”——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: as a way, you know—we see China as now the justification for doing all these other things, a lot of which we were already doing, to just keep doing it. But they also see China as a useful tool to kind of refashion an American political consensus.
transcript.zh: 作为抓手——如今他们把中国当成推进其他诸多举措的正当理由，其中很多事其实我们原本就在做，只是借此继续做下去。但他们同时也把中国视为一种趁手的工具，试图借此重塑美国的政治共识。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Not just a foreign policy consensus, but they see it as a way to rebuild a broader political consensus. Now, I think that's dangerous, I think that's not going to work, and I think that's going to lead inevitably to conflict.
transcript.zh: 不只是外交政策共识，他们还想借此重建更广泛的国内政治共识。在我看来，这非常危险，也根本行不通，而且必然会把我们引向冲突。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And I would point to Senator Sanders' piece in Foreign Affairs back, I think it was, I don't know, March, April of 2021, that warned about this, saying we don't want a Cold War with China.
transcript.zh: 我想提到 Sanders 参议员在《外交事务》（Foreign Affairs）上发表的那篇文章——大概是2021年3月或4月吧——他当时就对此发出过警告，直言我们不希望与中国陷入冷战。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: It is a fantasy to believe that we can reconstitute or rebuild any kind of durable and meaningful and real consensus here in the United States on the basis of just hostility to any one country.
transcript.zh: 如果以为仅凭对某一个国家的敌意，就能在美国国内重新拼凑或建立起任何持久、有意义且真实的共识，那简直是痴人说梦。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And I think one of the important insights from that piece is, you know, the struggle between democracy and authoritarianism is not primarily happening between states; it's happening within states, including ours. It is happening within—
transcript.zh: 我认为那篇文章提出的一个重要洞见在于：民主与威权之间的斗争，主要并不是发生在国家与国家之间，而是发生在各个国家内部——包括我们自己国家在内。它就发生在——

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Including us, yeah. Yeah, I think Mike Brenes's book, with Van Jackson—
transcript.zh: 包括我们自己，没错。对，我想提一下 Mike Brenes 与 Van Jackson 合著的那本书——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Right. Yeah, The Rivalry Peril. Yeah, I agree, it's a really great book, and Mike and Van wrote the kind of prologue to the book I edited.
transcript.zh: 对，就是《The Rivalry Peril》。没错，我也觉得那是一本非常出色的书，而且 Mike 和 Van 还为我主编的这本书撰写了序言部分。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And I'm really glad they did that because it really kind of lays down, I guess, the vibe of the book. It's like we're not seeking competition; this kind of mania for sustaining American primacy will not make Americans safer or more prosperous.
transcript.zh: 我非常高兴他们能写这篇序言，因为它某种程度上为整本书定下了基调：我们并不追求竞争，这种执迷于维持美国主导地位的狂热，并不会让美国人变得更安全或更富裕。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So, and then let me just quickly run through the other two. You've got, I think, yes, the kind of restraint-oriented progressives, and I kind of describe myself as restraint-curious.
transcript.zh: 好，那我再快速过一下另外两个阵营。第二个，我想是的，就是倾向克制的进步派，我自己也算是对“克制派”颇感兴趣（restraint-curious）。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: You know, I mean, there's a lot about the restraint foreign policy that I agree with, but as a progressive, issues—as Samm raised earlier—like issues of human rights, democracy, these things matter a lot to me.
transcript.zh: 我是说，克制派外交政策中有很多主张我是认同的，但作为一名进步派，就像 Samm 刚才提到的，人权、民主这类议题对我来说依然非常重要。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So again, while I am modest about America's ability to create these realities abroad, I do think this should be a part of how America approaches the world—the idea that, you know, all human beings have certain rights.
transcript.zh: 所以同样地，虽然我对美国在海外塑造这些现实的能力持谦卑态度，但我确实认为，这应当成为美国看待和处理国际事务的一部分——也就是说，所有人都应当享有某些基本权利。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: The third piece is—and you started to get to this—you know, there is the anti-monopolist, which, you know, people like Rush Doshi, Matt Stoller, who I think have some very interesting things to say.
transcript.zh: 第三个阵营——你刚才也已经触及到了——就是反垄断派，像 Rush Doshi、Matt Stoller 这些人，我觉得他们提出的一些观点非常有意思。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I may differ from them in terms of how far they go in seeing China as a threat to the United States, but I do think where there is some agreement space between that trend—
transcript.zh: 在把中国视为对美国的威胁这件事上，他们走得有多远，我或许和他们存在分歧；但我确实认为，在这一思潮之间存在一定的共识空间——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: and there are a lot of labor folks who agree with them as well—but I think where the kind of agreement space is, is we all oppose concentrations of power, right?
transcript.zh: 而且也有很多劳工界人士认同他们的看法——但我认为，我们彼此的共识空间在于，我们都反对权力的过度集中，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Whether it's oligarchs and wealthy individuals and corporations concentrating power over Americans' political and economic life, or whether it's China concentrating power over supply chains that Americans rely on. And that's—
transcript.zh: 无论是寡头、富豪个人和大企业将权力集中在美国人的政治与经济生活之上，还是中国将权力集中在美方所依赖的供应链之上，都是如此。而这正是——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: you know, that in and of itself is not an anti-China play. I mean, I would oppose the concentration of power over supply chains, whether it was China or any country who was doing that.
transcript.zh: 要知道，这本身并不是针对中国的反华操作。我是说，无论是中国还是其他任何国家在供应链上集中权力，我都会反对。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: It just so happens that China has decided this is a part of dependencies that they want to create to advance the Chinese government's interests as they define them.
transcript.zh: 只是恰巧中国决定将其作为他们想要建立的依赖关系的一部分，以此来推进中国政府自身所界定的利益。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Even if it was done defensively, mainly, I mean as a reaction, right?
transcript.zh: 即便这主要是出于防御目的，我是说作为一种被动反应，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: That's right. You know, again, any country is going to seek advantage and use those things defensively or just generally to sustain and advance their own interests.
transcript.zh: 没错。要知道，再说一遍，任何国家都会寻求优势，并把这些手段用于防御，或者泛泛地说，用来维系和推进自身利益。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: That's a good taxonomy. It's a very interesting one, yeah.
transcript.zh: 这个分类法很好，非常有趣，是的。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: In the taxonomy of the left, do you think that there has been a shift? You know, in 2024, you gave a speech in Beijing at the Xiangshan Forum, and then you were saying, there is no Washington consensus on China, right?
transcript.zh: 在左翼内部的谱系划分中，你认为是否出现了某种转向？2024年你在北京香山论坛发表过一次演讲，当时你就提到，华盛顿在对华问题上并不存在共识，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: You have these different positions, whether it's the great power camp, whether it's the restrainers, whether it's the defenders of the old primacy.
transcript.zh: 当时存在不同的立场派别，无论是大国竞争派、克制派，还是旧主导地位的捍卫者。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Has there been any realignment in these different sort of taxonomies of the left?
transcript.zh: 在左翼内部这些不同的派别划分中，现在是否发生了某种重新洗牌？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean, it's a good question.
transcript.zh: 我是说，这是个好问题。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Especially after Trump's détente, yeah, I mean—
transcript.zh: 尤其是在特朗普开启缓和之后，是啊，我是说——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: No, but I would, you know, continue to agree with myself. There is, as of right now, I mean, again, the establishment remains the establishment, as I said before.
transcript.zh: 不会，不过我还是会继续赞同我自己的判断。截至目前，我的意思是，正如我之前所说，建制派依然还是那个建制派。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: You know, the high church of foreign policy, even though it is under serious criticism, is still very invested in sustaining American global hegemony, global primacy, even if just for its own sake.
transcript.zh: 外交政策界的正统派虽然正遭受严厉批评，但依然极力投入于维系美国的全球霸权与全球主导地位，哪怕仅仅是为了霸权本身。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Going back, there was this phrase that former Secretary of State Antony Blinken used to use in multiple speeches where he was like,
transcript.zh: 回溯来看，前国务卿Antony Blinken过去常在多场演讲中用到这样一句话，他的意思是，

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: you know, if America's not at the table shaping the global agenda, then someone else will, someone who's hostile to us, or even worse, no one will, and it'll just be chaos.
transcript.zh: 如果美国不在谈判桌上主导全球议程，就会有别人来主导——一个对我们怀有敌意的人——甚至更糟的是，无人主导，世界将陷入一片混乱。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: It's just this idea that if America is not at every table shaping the agenda to its interests, it will all fall into chaos.
transcript.zh: 核心就是这样一种观念：如果美国不能在每张谈判桌上按照自身利益塑造议程，一切就会陷入混乱。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: That is still a pretty powerful instinct among the foreign policy graybeards in the United States, and a lot of people who've been kind of mentored by those graybeards.
transcript.zh: 在美国的外交政策界元老以及许多受这些元老提携指导的人士当中，这依然是一种相当强烈的本能。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But again, in part thanks to Donald Trump—and that is not a sentence I say often—the consensus has not really solidified yet about what the U.S.-China relationship should look like.
transcript.zh: 但同样，部分要归功于唐纳德·特朗普——这句话我可不常说——关于美中关系究竟应该是什么样子，目前共识尚未真正固化。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And my view is like, that will not last. I mean, everyone is kind of urgently trying to imprint their own preferences on what that relationship will look like into the future.
transcript.zh: 而我的看法是，这种状态不会持久。我是说，各方都在急切地试图将自己的偏好烙印到美中关系未来的走向之中。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So I would like it to be one that really does prioritize coexistence, that really does prioritize peace, without turning a blind eye to the important issues that Samm brought up at the beginning.
transcript.zh: 所以我希望最终成形的是一种真正将共处放在首位、真正将和平放在首位的关系，同时也不回避Samm在开头提到的那些重要议题。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: One thing that I think we have seen a shift in, or world events have intensified, right, have been foreign incursions abroad. And for the progressives, you know, they've really been galvanized in the events post-October 7th.
transcript.zh: 我认为有一件事已经发生了转向，或者说被国际局势所加剧了，那就是海外军事介入。对进步派而言，10月7日之后的一系列事件真正激发了他们的动员。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Already, you know, this generation of progressives was really created by the response to Iraq. So how do you see China fitting into that template, right?
transcript.zh: 而且要知道，这一代进步派本来就是在对伊拉克战争的回应中成长起来的。那么你认为中国该如何嵌入这个框架之中呢？

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Because in some ways it's kind of its own entity in that dynamic. Where is China in that playbook?
transcript.zh: 因为在某种程度上，中国在这种互动格局中算是一个自成一体的存在。在这套剧本里，中国处于什么位置？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Well, it's interesting. I mean, I don't know if this answers your question fully, but I think a lot of progressives who kind of came into this work, politics or foreign policy, in the wake of Iraq—
transcript.zh: 嗯，这很有意思。我是说，我不确定这能否完全回答你的问题，但我认为许多在伊拉克战争之后投身政治或外交政策工作的进步派人士——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: —and in this I include myself as well, even though, interestingly, my initial engagement in politics and political activism was through the alter-globalization movement of the late '90s and early 2000s—
transcript.zh: ——其中也包括我自己，尽管有趣的是，我最初参与政治和政治行动是通过上世纪90年代末至本世纪初的另类全球化运动——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: —you know, protesting the World Bank, IMF, the WTO, which definitely relates to China in an interesting way.
transcript.zh: ——就是去抗议世界银行、IMF和WTO，这无疑以一种有趣的方式与中国产生关联。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But to go to the Iraq question, I think it has kind of inculcated this really deep suspicion of grand crusades and like existential threats—
transcript.zh: 但回到伊拉克问题上，我认为它确实灌输了一种根深蒂固的怀疑态度，即对宏大十字军式远征以及所谓‘生存性威胁’的怀疑——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: —the idea that, oh, this threat is so different and so dire that it is just an unprecedented thing, and the old lessons—we have to take this so much more seriously.
transcript.zh: ——也就是那种论调：哦，这个威胁截然不同、极其严峻，简直前所未有，过去的教训不再适用，我们必须极其严肃地对待它。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I just, I think that's just so silly. Because if you go back—
transcript.zh: 我只是觉得，这实在是太荒谬了。因为如果你回过头去看——

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: That's a really important insight, yeah.
transcript.zh: 这是一个非常重要的洞见，是的。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: It's like every threat is treated that way, whether, you know, whether it's the Soviet Union, whether it was, you know, terrorism.
transcript.zh: 仿佛每一个威胁都会被这样对待，不管是过去的苏联，还是后来的恐怖主义，都是如此。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And let's remember, going back to the '90s, you know, when the foreign policy establishment was casting about for a new justification for itself after the collapse of the Soviet Union, it was going to be China.
transcript.zh: 别忘了，回到上世纪90年代，当苏联解体后外交政策建制派四处寻找自身存在的新理由时，那个靶子原本就是中国。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean, there was a concerted effort to make China—they were going to slot out USSR and just slot in China. And in the early days of the George W. Bush administration, I mean, it looked like we were on path.
transcript.zh: 我是说，当时有一股协同一致的努力想把中国塑造成这样——他们打算把苏联拿掉，直接把中国填进去。而在乔治·W·布什政府初期，看起来我们确实正走在这样的轨道上。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: You had the Hainan Island incident, where this, you know, the collision of the two—of the American surveillance plane and the Chinese—
transcript.zh: 当时发生了海南岛事件，也就是美国侦察机与中国——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: ...plane, and things were getting pretty tense, and one can easily imagine that they continued to get worse, but then 9/11 happened. Everyone was like, "No, no, no, no, we're slotting out USSR, we're slotting in terrorism."
transcript.zh: ……飞机，当时局势已经变得相当紧张，我们完全可以想象事态本会继续恶化，但随后“9·11”事件发生了。所有人立刻转而表示：“不不不，我们要把苏联拿掉，把恐怖主义填进去。”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And then we spent the next two-plus decades making foreign policy all about that. Two decades that China really used to its advantage when we were investing enormous attention and resources into fighting essentially a few hundred, if that, religious extremists.
transcript.zh: 此后二十多年里，我们的外交政策几乎完全围绕着反恐展开。而当我们把大量精力和资源投入到打击不过区区几百名——甚至可能还不到这个数字的——宗教极端分子时，中国则充分把握住了这二十年的战略机遇。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, that's definitely how I tell the story, although I would focus on the first six or seven years right after September 11th. And note that there really wasn't anything that roiled the waters between China and the US during that wonderful period.
transcript.zh: 没错，我也是这么讲述这段历史的，不过我会把重点放在“9·11”事件刚过去后的头六七年。必须指出，在那段难得的时期里，中美之间几乎没有什么真正激起波澜的事件。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And China went into a period of real internal loosening as well, which was, I think, a fun time to live here.
transcript.zh: 与此同时，中国国内也进入了一个相对宽松的时期，我想那段日子住在中国确实很有意思。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I want to ask you—I don't like the word expertise when it comes to China—but I wonder whether the left has enough China expertise, as it were, to staff an administration. I mean, do we have a bench?
transcript.zh: 我想问你——谈到中国问题时，我不太喜欢用“专业知识”这个词——但我不禁想，美国左翼是否拥有足够多的“中国通”或相关人才储备来组建一届政府班底？我的意思是，我们有足够的人才梯队吗？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, we like folks like Van Jackson and Jake Werner and Michael Brenes. We all esteem them, I imagine. But are there other folks who you'd like seen brought in, or at least, you know, to meet with candidates, to meet with progressive Dems?
transcript.zh: 我是说，我们都很欣赏 Van Jackson、Jake Werner 和 Michael Brenes 这样的人，我想大家对他们都很敬重。但除此之外，还有哪些人是你希望看到被吸纳进来的，或者至少能与候选人、与进步派民主党人会面交流的？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, I can think of several from the Obama administration and even some on the periphery of the Biden administration who are, you know, simpatico with progressives, very smart on China, wouldn't do too much damage, but I worry about the bench.
transcript.zh: 我能想到奥巴马政府时期的几个人，甚至还有拜登政府外围的一些人，他们对进步派颇有共鸣，对中国问题也很敏锐，不至于造成太大破坏，但我确实很担心整体的人才储备。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah, no, no, I mean, listen, this is a problem I think the left has more broadly than just China, right? The left is more powerful in the United States than it has ever been in my lifetime.
transcript.zh: 是的，听我说，我认为这是左翼在更广泛层面上面临的问题，而不仅仅局限于中国议题，对吧？如今美国左翼的力量比我有生以来的任何时候都要强大。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: It is getting and using political power, I think, in a more pragmatic and effective way.
transcript.zh: 我认为它正以一种更加务实和有效的方式获取并运用政治权力。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But still, in foreign policy in general, there is a scrappy coalition of foreign policy organizations, little think tanks, and advocacy groups that punch far above their weight, I think, in terms of impacting the debate.
transcript.zh: 但即便如此，就整个外交政策领域而言，目前仍只是由一批外交政策机构、小型智库和倡导团体组成了一个充满拼劲的联盟，它们在影响政策辩论方面发挥着远超自身体量的作用。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: We've got more congressional champions than we've ever had coming from a progressive foreign policy perspective, but we still lack, I think, as you put it, a bench of folks who have served at those mid and higher levels such that could serve a progressive president.
transcript.zh: 我们在国会中拥有比以往任何时候都多、秉持进步派外交政策立场的推动者，但正如你所说，我们依然缺乏一个曾在中高层担任过职务、日后能够辅佐一位进步派总统的人才梯队。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So yeah, that's a problem I think about a lot. I think a lot of us do.
transcript.zh: 所以，这确实是我经常思考的问题，我想我们很多人都对此深有同感。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: In the best-case scenario where you had a progressive president that wanted to find a constructive way to coexist and engage with, and cooperate wherever possible and compete where necessary with China, that president would still have to reach beyond just kind of the left. I don't think there's any question.
transcript.zh: 在最理想的情况下，即便我们有了一位希望寻找建设性方式与中国共存、接触，在可能之处合作、在必要之处竞争的进步派总统，这位总统依然必须将选才范围扩大到左翼阵营之外。这一点毫无疑问。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But I also think what would need to happen here is that you would have a president who campaigned, ran, and won having promised a different relationship.
transcript.zh: 但我也认为，这里真正需要发生的是，有一位总统在竞选、参选并胜选的过程中，就曾承诺要建立一种不同的关系。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Having promised to seek not just a different relationship with China, but a different relationship with the world, and would come into office with a mandate to really change the paradigm.
transcript.zh: 承诺不仅要寻求一种不同的对华关系，而且要寻求一种不同的对世界关系，并带着真正改变既有范式的民意授权走马上任。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And to that, you know, and again, I mean, "personnel is policy" is one of those things you hear in Washington all the time. I think sometimes it's true, sometimes it's much less true.
transcript.zh: 说到这里，我们在华盛顿总能听到“人事即政策”这句话。我觉得这话有时是对的，有时则远远没那么准确。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But it's true really if you're talking about the president and maybe a dozen, a dozen and a half people who are working with that president.
transcript.zh: 不过，如果你指的是总统本人以及与总统共事的大约十几个人，那这句话确实成立。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So I think the key would be to have a president, yes, who was elected with a mandate to make some of these decisions, and to have a number of top people around them to help them execute it through the bureaucracy.
transcript.zh: 因此我认为关键在于，首先要有这样一位带着民意授权当选、敢于做出这类决断的总统，同时其身边还要有一批高层核心人员，协助其通过官僚体系来贯彻执行。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah. So Matt, you were very close to Senator Sanders. Can you talk about Bernie's arc when it comes to China?
transcript.zh: 是的。Matt，你曾与 Bernie Sanders 参议员关系非常密切。你能谈谈 Bernie 在中国问题上的立场演变轨迹吗？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, in 2000 he was opposed to PNTR, to permanent normalized trade relations. But in 2021, he wrote this great Foreign Affairs essay you alluded to, opposing a new Cold War, and I believe, you know, you were his advisor then.
transcript.zh: 我是说，2000年时他反对给予中国永久正常贸易关系（PNTR）。但到了2021年，他撰写了你刚才提到的那篇发表在《外交》（Foreign Affairs）上的重要文章，反对新冷战，而我记得你当时正是他的顾问。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Now he's involved with AI safety conversations with China, you know, at a very high level, which I really applaud. Help me understand his trajectory and what some of the things were that shaped it when it comes to China.
transcript.zh: 如今，他正在非常高的层面上参与对华 AI 安全对话，对此我非常赞赏。请帮我梳理一下他在中国问题上的思想演变轨迹，以及塑造这一轨迹的一些关键因素。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Well, during the '90s, he was very much aware of this movement that I was a part of as well.
transcript.zh: 嗯，在九十年代，他对当时我也身处其中的那场运动非常了解。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: That's where he came from as a kind of democratic socialist, opposed to the whole neoliberal model before it was cool.
transcript.zh: 他正是从那样的背景走出来的——作为一名民主社会主义者，早在反对新自由主义模式成为潮流之前，他就一直对此持反对立场。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean, the idea that if we only free capital, then, you know, everyone will get rich and everyone will be happy. I mean, he was calling bullshit on that for a very, very long time.
transcript.zh: 就是那种“只要给资本松绑，所有人就会富裕、所有人都会幸福”的论调。他很早以前就一直在戳穿这种鬼话。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And I think that is what undergirded his opposition to PNTR with China, just the idea that, okay, we should be a little bit more careful about that. But I think there—
transcript.zh: 我想，正是这种认知支撑了他当年反对给予中国永久正常贸易关系（PNTR）的立场，也就是认为我们在这件事上应该更加谨慎一些。但我认为……

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: The reason he brought that up in that Foreign Affairs piece is to say the consensus back then was just like wall-to-wall: "Oh yeah, we're going to give China this special new status, we'll let them into the WTO, everyone in China will get rich, and then obviously China will become more democratic."
transcript.zh: 他在《外交》杂志那篇文章里提到这一点，就是想说明当时的共识几乎一边倒地认为：“没错，我们要给中国这种特殊的新地位，让他们加入世贸组织，这样所有中国人都会富起来，然后中国显然就会变得更加民主。”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: This is just the way things work. And he was skeptical of that. And he was right.
transcript.zh: 仿佛事情理应如此。但他对此持怀疑态度，而且事实证明他是对的。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Now, again, we can point to—and you have both talked about things that happened between then and now where things could have gone perhaps a different way—but that turned out not to be true, yet everyone was absolutely convinced that this was just a force of nature.
transcript.zh: 当然，正如你们二位也探讨过的，从那时到现在发生了很多事，局势原本或许也有可能走向不同的方向；但不管怎样，当年的那种预设最终落空了，而当时所有人却笃定地以为那就像自然规律一样不可逆转。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: You know, in the words of Tony Blair, former UK Prime Minister, arguing against the neoliberal model was like arguing against the weather. It's just reality. And that was very silly.
transcript.zh: 就像英国前首相托尼·布莱尔说的那样，反对新自由主义模式就好比跟天气较劲——它就是客观现实。这种看法非常荒唐。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: That turned out to be false. And that is something I think most people recognize now, as I was saying about the Biden administration—they acknowledge, "Okay, yeah, all this old theology was not true."
transcript.zh: 事实证明这是错的。我想现在大多数人都意识到了这一点，就像我刚才谈到拜登政府时说的，他们也承认：“好吧，过去那套教条确实站不住脚。”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But he's using that, kind of like planting that flag, to say more or less: "Yeah, I was calling BS on the old consensus, and now I'm calling BS on what looks to be a quickly forming new consensus..."
transcript.zh: 但他借此亮明了自己的立场，意思大概就是：“当年我就在戳穿旧共识的鬼话，现在面对似乎正在迅速成型的新共识，我同样不买账……”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: "...which is that the US and China are destined to be locked into this competition, potentially conflict, for who gets to rule the world, and I don't support that. That's a bad idea. I don't think we should accept that framework for how the US and China will work together."
transcript.zh: “……也就是认定美中注定要陷入争夺世界主导权的竞争乃至潜在冲突之中。我不支持这种看法，这主意糟糕透顶。我不认为我们应该接受这种框架来定义美中未来的相处之道。”

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: One of the things that's given me great joy is looking at younger progressives and China. I've talked quite a bit about this vibe shift on China that seems to have started back in January 2025, around the time of Trump's inauguration...
transcript.zh: 最让我感到欣慰的一件事，就是观察年轻一代进步派人士对中国的态度。我此前也多次谈到过这股对华舆论氛围的转向，它似乎始于2025年1月特朗普就职前后……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: ...what with the release of DeepSeek, the TikTok refugee phenomenon when they all went tongue-in-cheek onto Xiaohongshu, RedNote. It's been borne out in survey after survey: young Americans, Gen Z especially, have a very different, much more positive view of China, or at least a much less negative view.
transcript.zh: ……当时恰逢DeepSeek发布，以及大批“TikTok难民”半开玩笑地涌入小红书（RedNote）。接连不断的民调也印证了这一点：美国年轻人，尤其是Z世代，对中国的看法已经大不相同，变得更加积极，至少负面观感大幅减少了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Is that registering for progressive politicians? Are they understanding now that China bashing isn't good electoral politics if they want to appeal to Gen Z?
transcript.zh: 进步派政客们意识到这种变化了吗？如果他们想争取Z世代的选票，他们现在是否明白，一味抨击中国并不是高明的选举策略？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean, I think they are. We've seen poll after poll—there were two particular polls a few months ago, I think one from Pew and one from the Chicago Council on Global Affairs...
transcript.zh: 我想他们是意识到了。我们看到一份又一份的民调——几个月前就有两项特别有代表性的调查，好像一项来自皮尤研究中心，另一项来自芝加哥全球事务委员会……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Exactly, that's right.
transcript.zh: 没错，正是如此。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: ...just showed, you know, Americans again, they don't seek conflict with China. They're not super concerned that China's going to come and eat their lunch.
transcript.zh: ……调查结果再次表明，美国民众并不希望与中国发生冲突，也并不特别担心中国会来抢走他们的饭碗。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And I think that's reflective of a general sense among Americans of just exhaustion. We've been in conflict with the world for decades now. We've been fighting these stupid, pointless, endless wars that have not really delivered anything for our communities.
transcript.zh: 我认为这反映出美国社会普遍存在的倦怠感。几十年来我们一直与世界处于冲突之中，一直在打那些愚蠢、毫无意义且没完没了的战争，而这些战争并没有给我们的社区带来任何实质回报。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And they've been expensive, and they've undercut our ability to advance our interests diplomatically. And I think that's good, but I would also note here, I think it's also a reflection of the way Trump has handled it.
transcript.zh: 这些战争不仅耗资巨大，还削弱了我们通过外交手段推进自身利益的能力。我觉得民众有这种倦怠感是好事，但同时我也想指出，这也折射出特朗普处理这一问题的方式。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean, Americans—people in general—are not super read in on the details of foreign policy. That is fine; that's not a value judgment. It's like people have more immediate concerns than us foreign policy nerds.
transcript.zh: 我的意思是，普通美国民众通常不会去深入了解外交政策的细节。这很正常，并非价值评判，大家都有比我们这些外交政策书呆子更迫切的现实关切。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Sure.
transcript.zh: 确实。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And so I think they tend to take cues on foreign policy from their leaders. And the cues Donald Trump has been sending is, "All right, let's just find a way to work with China. It's not a huge problem."
transcript.zh: 因此，他们往往会从领导人那里获取外交政策的风向信号。而特朗普传递出的信号是：“好吧，我们就找个办法和中国打交道，这算不上什么大问题。”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: He was sending very different cues in his first administration...
transcript.zh: 他在第一任期内传递的信号可大不相同……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Sure was.
transcript.zh: 那可真是。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: ...and I think you could look at the polls and see people responding to that. I like the cues he's been sending in his second term much, much better.
transcript.zh: ……我想从民调中就能看出，民众对此作出了回应。相比之下，我更喜欢他在第二任期内传递出的信号，要好得多。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Me too, me too.
transcript.zh: 我也是，我也是。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: So, you know, I want to pick back up on something you talked about before—that there's this alignment around opposition to concentrations of power.
transcript.zh: 那么，我想接着你之前提到的一个观点往下聊——也就是围绕“反对权力集中”正在形成某种共识。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: And I think something that's come to the fore in the wake of Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia and the fallout from that scandal is: well, what concentration of power are we opposing?
transcript.zh: 我认为，在黄仁勋重返英伟达掌舵以及那场风波的余波之后，一个日益凸显的问题是：我们究竟在反对哪一种权力集中？

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Because you've got the Nvidia concentration of power, but then you also have an Anthropic concentration of power. And there's been this kind of realignment around the hawkish consensus on those different concentrations of power.
transcript.zh: 因为一方面存在英伟达代表的权力集中，但另一方面也存在Anthropic代表的权力集中。围绕这两种不同的权力集中现象，鹰派共识似乎出现了某种重新站队。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: And I think before Nvidia blew up, it seemed like the hawkish consensus that was so dominant had broken in recognition of the very kind of ripple effects that you're talking about.
transcript.zh: 我觉得在英伟达事件爆发之前，原本占据主导地位的鹰派共识似乎已经瓦解，人们也开始意识到你刚才所说的那种连锁反应。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Do you think that that hawkish consensus that was so dominant—was it just dormant and now Nvidia has kind of reawakened it...
transcript.zh: 你认为那个曾经占据主导地位的鹰派共识，当时只是暂时蛰伏、如今又被英伟达事件重新唤醒了……

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: ...or is this something that we've really moved beyond? How do you think about the different sort of—
transcript.zh: ……还是说我们已经真正走出了那个阶段？你如何看待这些不同层面的——

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: debate surrounding opposition to concentrations of power and where China plays a role in that.
transcript.zh: ……围绕反对权力集中的争论，以及中国在其中扮演什么角色？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Well, again, I may not be fully understanding the question, but I'll just say this. I mean, what we saw with Jensen Huang was a very clear understanding from Donald Trump's point of view that inflation—to the extent that the economy is doing well, it's because of AI.
transcript.zh: 嗯，话说回来，我可能没有完全理解你的问题，但我先谈谈我的看法。我们在黄仁勋这件事上看到的，其实是特朗普非常明确的一个认知：就当前经济表现尚可的这部分而言，靠的就是人工智能。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And getting Jensen Huang back into Nvidia was going to be good for the stock market. That is really the only poll that matters to Donald Trump. And we saw the markets responding very, very positively to the reinstatement of Jensen Huang.
transcript.zh: 让黄仁勋重返英伟达对股市来说是件好事——而股市才是特朗普唯一关心的“民调”。我们也看到，市场对黄仁勋的回归作出了非常积极的反应。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And, you know, the AI bubble is really what's keeping the economy going, and Donald Trump recognizes that very clearly.
transcript.zh: 而且，支撑当前经济运转的其实就是AI泡沫，特朗普对此看得很清楚。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And what that gets to is like, yeah, these tech barons, these oligarchs, their companies continuing to profit and to kind of prop up the economy—that's just like an inappropriate amount of power that they have. But that's the way Donald Trump looks at the world.
transcript.zh: 而这背后的问题在于：没错，这些科技巨头、这些寡头，他们的公司持续获利并在某种程度上撑起了整个经济——他们掌握的权力实在过于庞大，很不恰当。但这正是特朗普看待世界的方式。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And not only Donald Trump. I mean, listen, we have worshiped the market.
transcript.zh: 而且不只是特朗普。听着，我们向来崇拜市场。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: The bond market has been determinative in so much of American foreign policy, keeping the stock market going and keeping people chilled out about their 401(k)s and their stock portfolios and their pensions.
transcript.zh: 债券市场在很大程度上左右着美国的外交政策，目的就是维持股市运转，让民众对自己的401(k)账户、股票投资组合和养老金感到安心。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And all this stuff matters, all right? That's part of American prosperity.
transcript.zh: 这些东西确实都很重要，没错，这是美国繁荣的一部分。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But I think this deference to the health of big business, especially these huge corporations, is really part of the challenge we face in strengthening our economy and battling corruption, battling oligarchy.
transcript.zh: 但我认为，对大型企业——尤其是这些超大型跨国公司——经营状况的过度顺从，正是我们在提振经济、打击腐败和对抗寡头政治时所面临挑战的一部分。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: So I just wanted to clarify for my question, which is: when we're talking about Nvidia and we're talking about Anthropic, I think it matters because the hawkish consensus in some ways has also coalesced around a different concentration of power—
transcript.zh: 我只是想把我的问题再澄清一下：当我们谈论英伟达和Anthropic时，之所以重要，是因为在某种意义上，鹰派共识也已经围绕另一种权力集中凝聚了起来——

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: —which is US companies like Anthropic that have been pounding the drumbeat of China as the existential threat, right? And so the hawkish consensus now can kind of be split between different corporate interests. So I just wanted to clarify that.
transcript.zh: ——也就是像Anthropic这样一直在鼓吹“中国是生存威胁”的美国公司，对吧？因此，如今的鹰派共识某种程度上可能会在不同企业利益集团之间发生分裂。我只是想澄清这一点。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah, no, no. I think it breaks down on whether people believe that the way to compete with China or advance American AI or win the AI race or win the future—and I don't even know what all this shit means, like 'win the future.'
transcript.zh: 对，没错。我认为这取决于人们是否相信，与中国竞争、推进美国AI发展、赢得AI竞赛乃至“赢得未来”——我甚至搞不懂这些鬼话到底是什么意思，比如“赢得未来”——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: What does that even mean, you know? 'America must win the future.' I think it's very, very silly. But it's this idea that, oh, we need to support these drugged-out evil nerds so they can win the AI race for America—
transcript.zh: 这到底算什么意思？“美国必须赢得未来。”我觉得这非常非常荒谬。但现在就有这么一种论调，说我们必须扶持这帮嗑药成瘾的邪恶极客，好让他们为美国赢下AI竞赛——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: —versus, you know, actually the way China—and it's very interesting, and you guys know this better than me—the way that China actually manages its AI companies: it's much more diverse, it's much more competitive,
transcript.zh: ——而反观中国实际管理本国AI企业的方式（这非常有意思，你们俩比我更了解），其实要多元化得多，竞争也激烈得多，

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: and yet these companies have advanced at great speed. So we have this very silly debate that, oh, we can't regulate our AI here;
transcript.zh: 但这些中国公司依然取得了突飞猛进的发展。所以，我们这边就出现了一种非常愚蠢的争论，说什么“我们不能在这里监管自己的AI；

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: we need to let these companies just do what they will, unfettered by pressure from the government, or else China will overtake us. That makes zero sense.
transcript.zh: 我们必须放任这些公司为所欲为，不受政府压力的束缚，否则中国就会超越我们。”这简直毫无道理。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Matt, in your initial response, though, you were sort of, I think, hinting at something that a lot of people see as the master key to understanding Trump's behavior, not just on China, basically on everything, and that is corruption.
transcript.zh: Matt，不过在你最初的回答里，我觉得你似乎点出了很多人眼中的一把“万能钥匙”——它不仅能解释特朗普对华政策的逻辑，几乎能解释他的一切行为，那就是“腐败”。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's not just the overall health of the American economy that he cares about; it's the health of the Trump family, the Trump Organization, and all their flunkies, yeah.
transcript.zh: 他关心的不只是美国经济的整体健康，而是特朗普家族、特朗普集团以及他们一众跟班的利益。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, yeah, you've definitely been known to apply this lens. I mean, it's part of your piece in Foreign Affairs. Is that what you see when you think about the China deals that Trump is going for?
transcript.zh: 没错，你向来以这一视角分析问题而闻名，这也是你在《外交事务》（Foreign Affairs）那篇文章里的核心观点之一。当你看待特朗普试图达成的那些对华交易时，你看到的也是这一面吗？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah, I would say this is part of everything Donald Trump is doing. This is part of everything that his sons are doing. I mean, Donnie Jr. is out there saying openly—I've heard this from multiple people—
transcript.zh: 是的，我认为这是特朗普所作所为的一部分，也是他儿子们所做一切的一部分。Donnie Jr. 就在外面公开宣称——我从好几个人那里都听到过这种说法——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: that his goal is to make sure the Trump family is one of the wealthiest families in the country by the end of Donald Trump's second term, which is just—I mean, the fact that he says this openly is crazy.
transcript.zh: 他的目标是确保到特朗普第二任期结束时，特朗普家族成为全美最富有的家族之一。说实话，他竟然能把这种话公开说出来，简直太疯狂了。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: You've got Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner out there as special envoys for everything apparently.
transcript.zh: 你看现在 Steve Witkoff 和 Jared Kushner 几乎成了包揽一切事务的特使。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: You know, they'll go in and spend 20 minutes checking boxes on whatever the issue is at hand, and then they'll get down to talking about, okay, what deals can we cut, what resorts are we going to open?
transcript.zh: 他们去到某个地方，先花二十分钟走过场似地应付一下眼前的议题，然后就直奔主题，开始谈：好吧，我们能签什么交易？打算在哪里开度假村？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: You know, the Gaza Board of Peace is a perfect example of this. It's all just a way to shake the tree and feather their own nest.
transcript.zh: 加沙和平委员会（Gaza Board of Peace）就是一个绝佳的例子。这一切不过是借机敛财、中饱私囊的手段罢了。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And again, it's blatant, but I think this is a problem that is much bigger and longer-standing than Donald Trump. I mean, what I've said repeatedly is like, Donald Trump...
transcript.zh: 而且再次强调，这种做法虽然赤裸裸，但我认为这是一个比特朗普本人更庞大、也存在得更久远的问题。正如我反复说过的，特朗普……

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: He is just the most blatant expression of pathologies that have existed in our politics for a long time. Donald Trump's talent is kind of turning the subtext into text.
transcript.zh: 他只是把我们政治体制中长期存在的种种病灶以最赤裸的方式表现了出来。特朗普的“本事”就在于把潜台词直接摆上台面。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: There was a measure of shame and kind of, you know, bashfulness about corruption before Donald Trump, but he just does it, right? He's just like, "Oh yeah, I'm here to line my own pockets."
transcript.zh: 在特朗普之前，政客们对腐败多少还存有一丝羞耻心，还会遮遮掩掩，但他却毫不掩饰，对吧？他简直就像在明说：“没错，我就是来中饱私囊的。”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But this has been a problem in American politics for a long, long time, and I think the fact that Trump is so blatant about it does give us an opportunity to discuss the fact that, you know, our campaign finance system is essentially a form of legalized bribery.
transcript.zh: 但这在美国政治中早已是一个积重难返的老问题了。我认为，特朗普把这一切做得如此露骨，反而给了我们一个契机，去正视这样一个事实：我们的竞选资金制度本质上就是一种合法化的贿赂。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: The fact that wealthy corporations and individuals enjoy enormous and inappropriate power over our political and economic life.
transcript.zh: 也就是富裕的企业和个人对我们的政治与经济生活享有极其庞大且极不相称的权力。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean, this is the core of our—as I see it—our political crisis, is that people who are well connected, very wealthy, and very influential get to play by a different set of rules than the rest of us.
transcript.zh: 在我看来，这正是我们政治危机的核心所在：那些人脉通天、家财万贯、极具影响力的人，可以按照一套与我们普通人截然不同的规则行事。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And this creates real and legitimate grievances on the part of people who are struggling, who are facing all kinds of other challenges, which in turn, you know, creates opportunities for demagogues like Donald Trump.
transcript.zh: 这在那些苦苦挣扎、面临种种困境的民众心中催生了真实而正当的不满，而这种不满反过来又为特朗普这样的煽动家创造了可乘之机。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And this is one of the real ironies of Trump, is that he is someone who has benefited from this double standard.
transcript.zh: 特朗普身上真正讽刺的地方之一就在于，他本人正是这种双重标准的既得利益者。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: He is, of course, very much a part of the elite, but he has also very effectively exploited grievances against it and presented himself as, you know, kind of an instrument of vengeance against an out-of-touch and self-dealing elite while being the most self-dealing president you could possibly imagine.
transcript.zh: 他当然是不折不扣的精英阶层一员，但他却极其老练地利用了民众对精英阶层的不满，把自己塑造成向脱离群众、以权谋私的精英阶层实施报复的工具——而与此同时，他自己却堪称史上最赤裸裸以权谋私的总统。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Well said.
transcript.zh: 说得好。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Looking beyond Trump, there's going to be—and I fear this—this temptation among Democrats to run to the right on China in 2028, right?
transcript.zh: 把目光放到特朗普之后，我其实很担心，到了2028年，民主党内部会出现一种在对华议题上向右转的冲动，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Let's out-hawk whoever the GOP candidate is, although that's hard to imagine how you out-hawk someone like Marco Rubio.
transcript.zh: 就是想着“无论共和党候选人是谁，我们都要比他更鹰派”——虽然我很难想象怎么才能比Marco Rubio这样的人更鹰派。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: But what are you advising, or how are you going to advise candidates to resist that temptation?
transcript.zh: 但你会如何建议，或者说你打算怎么劝说候选人去抵制这种诱惑？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah, I know, this is like one of my personal bugaboos. I mean, this is a very long-standing, you know, tendency among a lot of Democrats, especially older Democrats,
transcript.zh: 是啊，我明白，这算是我个人最反感的问题之一了。很多民主党人，尤其是老一辈民主党人，长期以来一直有这种倾向，

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: just like they really delight in being able to attack Republicans from the right on foreign policy. And, you know, what I think is that it's just—they need to break that habit.
transcript.zh: 仿佛能从右翼立场去攻击共和党的外交政策，会让他们感到莫大的快意。但我认为，他们必须改掉这个毛病。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Because what this does—and we saw this repeatedly in the last 25 years, and even going back farther—is that this just kind of reinforces a frame of hawkishness and conflict.
transcript.zh: 因为这样做只会不断强化鹰派对抗的叙事框架——这一点我们在过去25年乃至更长的时间里已经反复见识过了。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And add to that—your question about Marco Rubio is a good one—you will never out-nationalist the right. I mean, they will always like raise you. They will always raise and re-raise whatever dumb hawkish bullshit you're going to put on the table.
transcript.zh: 更何况——你刚才提到Marco Rubio是个很好的问题——你在民族主义立场上永远不可能比右翼更极端。无论你抛出什么愚蠢的鹰派强硬言辞，他们永远会加码、再加码，把你比下去。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So maybe just recognize that that game is not worth playing.
transcript.zh: 所以或许早该认清，这种游戏根本不值得去玩。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, it's a mug's game.
transcript.zh: 没错，那是自讨苦吃的愚蠢游戏。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And it's funny, like if you ask what the policy should be, here I'll go back to something Joe Biden himself said—I think it was early in the 2020 primary, it may have been like even early in 2019—where he was asked some question about China.
transcript.zh: 说起来挺有意思，如果你问政策到底该怎么做，我倒想引述拜登本人早年说过的一句话——大概是在2020年党内初选初期，甚至可能是2019年初——当时有人向他提了个关于中国的问题。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And he gave this really great Joe Biden answer where he was just like, "Oh, come on, Jack. You know, everybody's freaking out about China like they're going to eat our lunch. They're not going to eat our lunch. We can handle it."
transcript.zh: 他给出了一个非常典型的拜登式精彩回答，大意是：“得了吧，老兄。大家都在为中国惊慌失措，好像他们马上就要抢走我们的饭碗一样。他们抢不走我们的饭碗，我们应付得来。”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And I think that's like the best way to—that's a great way to talk about it. You know, yeah, sure, China is powerful, it's influential...
transcript.zh: 我觉得这才是谈论这个话题最好的方式。当然，中国很强大，也很有影响力……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's a little copium, but...
transcript.zh: 这听起来有点像是“精神安慰剂”（copium），不过……

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean, it's copium, but like, I just think talking about it in a way that's confident to say, "Listen, the United States remains pretty powerful. We've got a strong economy, a strong military, we have a set of relationships and alliances and engagements that China still cannot match."
transcript.zh: 好吧，就算有点自我安慰的成分，但我觉得关键在于要用一种自信的姿态去谈论它：“听着，美国依然非常强大。我们拥有强劲的经济、强大的军队，以及一整套中国至今仍无法企及的伙伴关系、同盟体系和国际布局。”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So let's just calm down and have a smart, rational conversation about how to advance our interests and what the relationship with China should look like.
transcript.zh: 所以，让我们先冷静下来，以明智、理性的方式探讨该如何推进美国自身的利益，以及美中关系应当呈现何种面貌。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Hopefully we have a choice beyond either inhaling huge plumes of copium or just entering full-blown moral panic. These are not attractive options.
transcript.zh: 但愿除了大口吸食“精神安慰剂”或彻底陷入道德恐慌之外，我们还有别的选项。这两种选择可都不怎么体面。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Look, I mean, I'm not the only person to have wondered why your post-midterms essay in Foreign Affairs didn't so much as mention China. So now I finally get to ask you some, you know, concrete questions about the next two years before the election.
transcript.zh: 说实话，在中期选举后你在《外交》（Foreign Affairs）杂志发表的那篇文章里，对华问题只字未提，我肯定不是唯一对此感到好奇的人。现在我终于有机会向你提几个关于大选前这两年的具体问题了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: What should and shouldn't the new Democratic-dominated Congress do? There's the future of the Select Committee, there's the National Defense Authorization Act,
transcript.zh: 民主党占主导地位的新一届国会应当做什么、不应当做什么？比如特设委员会的去留，还有《国防授权法案》，

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: you know, there's China always being cited as a sort of standing justification for defense budgets. And there's of course a lot more on chip export controls and things like that.
transcript.zh: 你知道，中国总是被当作提高国防预算的常备理由。当然，在芯片出口管制之类的问题上也还有很大文章可做。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I'll let Samm talk about that in a bit, but what about—let's concretely—the Select Committee, where do you stand on that?
transcript.zh: 芯片这块我一会儿让Samm来跟你聊，我们先谈个具体的：关于特设委员会，你持什么立场？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Well, let me just go back to the Foreign Affairs piece first. I mean, it's a legit question. Others—other friends and colleagues—have asked like, "Well, why wasn't this in it? Why wasn't that..."
transcript.zh: 嗯，先让我回应一下关于《外交》那篇文章的问题。这确实是个很合理的问题，其他朋友和同事也问过我：“为什么没写这个？为什么没写那个……”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: in it? And again, I wanted to just focus very, very—have a very small target list in terms of what I think is most urgent for the new Congress to do, and even what Democrats should do in the lame duck.
transcript.zh: ……里面没写什么？”再说一遍，我当时只是想高度聚焦——列出一份非常精简的目标清单，也就是我认为新一届国会最紧迫要做的事，甚至包括民主党人在“跛脚鸭”会期期间该采取的行动。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean, that's where I talked about the Iran war, urging Democrats to really threaten a shutdown, to offer, of course, a continuing resolution that prohibits any funds for the Iran war, but also to, you know, prepare to investigate corruption.
transcript.zh: 我在文章里谈到了伊朗战争，敦促民主党人真正以政府停摆相要挟，当然还要提出一份禁止将任何资金用于伊朗战争的持续拨款决议，同时也要准备好对腐败问题展开调查。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
