transcript.en: So, you know, the answer is just that I wanted to keep the kind of list of recommendations small and most urgent as I saw it. Obviously, China is a huge issue that Congress should and will dig into when they're back in 2027.
transcript.zh: 所以，答案其实就是我想把我眼中最紧迫的建议清单尽量精简。显然，中国是一个重大议题，等到2027年新一届国会复会时，他们应当也会深入研究这个问题。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So getting to your point on the Select Committee, I expect it will be renewed. Ro Khanna will very likely be the chair.
transcript.zh: 回到你关于特设委员会的问题，我预计它会继续保留。Ro Khanna 极有可能担任主席。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And it's interesting, because my initial reaction to it was, okay, even agreeing to the creation of a Select Committee is kind of an acquiescence to a hawkish China paradigm—
transcript.zh: 这很有意思，因为我最初的反应是：好吧，哪怕只是同意设立一个特设委员会，某种程度上也是对对华鹰派范式的默认——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: this idea that this threat is so urgent that we cannot rely on the regular order of just, you know, the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, as if the problem is so urgent that they can't just deal with it as they deal with a whole range of other issues.
transcript.zh: 也就是认为这种威胁紧迫到我们无法依赖常规议事程序，不能只靠众议院外交事务委员会、参议院外交关系委员会，仿佛这个问题紧急到他们无法像处理其他一系列议题那样去应对。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I still tend to think that's the case. However, as I've looked more into it and spoken to colleagues, including colleagues who worked closely with the committee,
transcript.zh: 我仍然倾向于认为情况确实如此。不过，随着我对此事了解得更深入，也和一些同事——包括曾与该委员会密切共事的同事——交流之后，

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: you know, I do see some value in having a committee that is able to look at the broad scope of the relationship—
transcript.zh: 我确实看到设立这样一个委员会的价值，它能够从更广泛的维度审视双边关系的全局——

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: whether it's labor, whether it's human rights, any number of issues—they have a remit that allows them to kind of look at all of these things holistically that perhaps the other committees don't.
transcript.zh: 无论是劳工问题、人权问题，还是其他任何议题——它的职权范围允许它以一种整体性的视角来审视所有这些问题，而其他委员会或许并不具备这种条件。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And I think if you had someone, or more than one person, a number of people on the committee who were committed to seeking a path of coexistence, that could potentially be helpful.
transcript.zh: 而且我认为，如果委员会里能有人——或者不止一个人，而是一批成员——致力于寻求一条共存之道，那或许会带来积极作用。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So again, I'm not answering the question firmly. I'm just saying I am intrigued by the idea that this committee could be put to some good use.
transcript.zh: 所以再次说明，我并不是给出一个斩钉截铁的回答。我只是说，我对这个委员会或许能发挥积极作用这一想法很感兴趣。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Okay.
transcript.zh: 好的。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: Let's talk about industrial policy for a moment. You know, I think that especially coming out of the midterms, we had a clearer sense of what the mandate is from the American public.
transcript.zh: 我们来谈谈产业政策吧。尤其是在中期选举刚结束的当下，我们对美国公众赋予的执政授权有了更清晰的认识。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: And one of the things that's becoming increasingly clear is that voters will accept industrial policy in some form.
transcript.zh: 而越来越明确的一点是，选民会接受某种形式的产业政策。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: And the question is, can we do this in a way that doesn't always play the China card? Do we need a foreign threat to acknowledge the importance of the role of government in industrial development?
transcript.zh: 问题在于，我们能否在推进产业政策时不总是打“中国牌”？我们难道非要借助一个外部威胁，才能承认政府在产业发展中所扮演角色的重要性吗？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean, I think we absolutely can. But I think the key is that Americans feel it, and that's where the challenge is.
transcript.zh: 我认为我们完全可以做到。但关键在于让美国民众切身感受到成效，而这正是挑战所在。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I think if you front-load steps—infrastructure rebuilding, things that people actually see in their communities—I think there's some benefit there.
transcript.zh: 我觉得如果你把一些举措前置——比如基础设施重建，也就是人们在自己社区里实实在在看得到的东西——这会带来实实在在的益处。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But even that aside, I don't think it's that hard for American leaders to come to the American people and say, you know, "The reason we're going to fix that bridge is not because it helps compete with China."
transcript.zh: 即便抛开这一点不谈，我认为美国领导人走到民众面前这样说其实并不难：“我们要修那座桥，并不是为了帮着和中国竞争。”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: "It's because we don't want you to fall through the f***ing bridge," you know, and into the icy river. Just as a joke, but it's also like, listen, we need to do these things because it's good for America, period.
transcript.zh: “而是因为我们不想让你们从那该死的桥上掉进冰冷的河里。”这固然是句玩笑话，但道理也是如此：听着，我们必须做这些事，就是因为这对美国有益，仅此而已。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Not because it will help us win the future against China—again, that ridiculous kind of framing.
transcript.zh: 而不是为了帮我们在与中国争夺未来的竞争中获胜——又是那种荒谬的叙事框架。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: But that may seem laughable to us, that, you know, "We don't want you to fall through the f***ing bridge" doesn't have anything to do with China. And yet we're at a moment now where even that requires playing the China card if you want to get it done.
transcript.zh: 但在我们看来这或许很可笑——“不想让你们从那该死的桥上掉下去”明明跟中国毫无关系。然而我们现在却处于这样一个时刻：哪怕连这种事，想办成也得打“中国牌”。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Well, I mean, it does for some, but I also think a lot of politicians just see it as a way to press the easy button, you know? This is how I can just get things through.
transcript.zh: 嗯，对有些人来说确实如此，但我也认为很多政客只是把这当成按下一个“省事按钮”，明白吗？觉得“我只要这么说就能把法案推过去”。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean, we went through this whole thing in the War on Terror too: everything is about fighting terror. You know, "We need to build this factory in my community because it helps us fight terror."
transcript.zh: 我们在“反恐战争”时期也经历过完全一样的事情：一切都与反恐挂钩。比如：“我们必须在我的选区建这座工厂，因为这有助于我们打击恐怖主义。”

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: You know, I mean, there's a tendency to see it as politically advantageous.
transcript.zh: 我的意思是，人们往往倾向于认为这么做在政治上更有利。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I just think politicians should be more courageous and level with the American people: we're just doing these things because they are actually good for us, without having to justify it in terms of kind of this foreign peril.
transcript.zh: 我只是觉得政客们应该更有勇气，向美国民众坦诚相告：我们做这些事纯粹是因为它们对我们自身确实有益，而不必非得借某种“外部威胁”来为之背书。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So Matt, I want to pivot and talk a little bit about the big foreign policy issue that Democrats will have to confront when it comes to talking about China.
transcript.zh: 那么 Matt，我想转换一下话题，聊聊民主党人在谈及中国时必须直面的那个重大外交政策议题。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: AOC, when she was at the Munich Security Conference, got asked this question on Taiwan, and she, you know, sort of infamously paused for a long time before, you know, she said—and I don't think she
transcript.zh: AOC 在参加慕尼黑安全会议时被问到了关于台湾的问题，她当时，怎么说呢，出了名地停顿了很长时间，然后才开口——而且我觉得她并没有

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: ...was wrong, you know, we want to make sure we never get to that point, right? That point being, you know, an actual confrontation.
transcript.zh: （我觉得她并没有）说错，我们确实希望确保永远不要走到那一步，对吧？那一步指的就是真正爆发对抗。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: In your opinion, what would have been the right way to respond to that? What should a progressive candidate have answered—the same thing just quicker, or...
transcript.zh: 依你之见，当时怎样回应才算恰当？一位进步派候选人应该怎么回答——还是同样的内容只是说得更快一点，还是……

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Yeah. Exactly. Yeah, I mean, and listen, you know, I was in the room for that. In the moment, I was like, okay, she took a minute, a few seconds, to answer a question of enormous consequence.
transcript.zh: 对，没错。说真的，听着，我当时就在现场。在那个当下我的反应是，好吧，她花了一小会儿——几秒钟的时间——来回答一个事关重大后果的问题。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Nothing wrong with that.
transcript.zh: 这完全没什么不对的。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Exactly. I mean, again, I said that and I'll say it now. It's like, frankly, you know, you've got all these members of Congress who pop off with all kinds of bullshit about, you know, wars and how we need to do this and that, and, you know, I mean, it's so tiresome and so irresponsible.
transcript.zh: 正是如此。我当时就这么说，现在也还是这么说。坦率讲，国会里有那么多议员动不动就对战争以及“我们必须这样、必须那样”大放厥词，说一堆废话，这实在是太令人厌烦，也太不负责任了。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And the idea, you know, and again, I'm close to this, but the idea that she took all this grief for like taking a few seconds to share thoughts on a potentially global conflict, I just find, you know, really, really frustrating.
transcript.zh: 而且——虽然我跟这件事也有点近身关联——但就因为她花了几秒钟斟酌如何回应一场可能演变为全球冲突的议题，就招致这么多非议，我实在觉得非常令人沮丧。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But yeah, I mean, she gave the right answer. So I might have just given it, you know, I would say, okay, give that like one or two seconds earlier. But still, that's the right answer.
transcript.zh: 但总的来说，她给出了正确的答案。要说有什么改进，我可能会早个一两秒把话说出来。不过归根结底，那就是正确的答案。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean, we should find ways to de-escalate, you know, to make sure we don't get on a path of conflict here. You know, from my view, this deeply unsatisfying status quo is probably the best we've got.
transcript.zh: 我的意思是，我们应当寻找给局势降温的办法，确保我们不会走上冲突的道路。在我看来，这个虽极其令人不满的现状，或许已经是我们能拥有的最好局面了。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Let's try to maintain our One China policy while also making clear that we support, you know, any resolution of this disagreement should be done peacefully, not militarily.
transcript.zh: 我们应努力维持我们的“一个中国”政策，同时明确表态：我们支持任何对这一分歧的解决都必须以和平方式而非军事手段实现。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But in the meantime, let's just try to keep things as chill as possible, to signal to China that we're not making precipitous moves. That does not exclude continuing to work with Taiwan and to also help Taiwan prepare to defend itself if need be.
transcript.zh: 但在此期间，我们应该尽量让局势保持冷静可控，向中国释放我们不会采取鲁莽举措的信号。这并不排除继续与台湾开展合作，也不排除在必要时协助台湾做好自卫准备。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But let's try to do this in as unprovocative a way as possible. And again, that's a tough line to walk, but here I'm guided by, you know, what I heard from progressive colleagues in Taipei when I was there earlier this year.
transcript.zh: 但我们要尽量以不具挑衅性的方式去做这些事。诚然，这之间的分寸很难拿捏，但在这一点上，我受到今年早些时候在台北时听到的进步派同行观点的启发。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Or no, I think it might have been even, shoot, I've lost track of time, it might have been last year. But anyway, within the last year and a half, I was in Taipei and met, you know, very progressive activists, very pro-independence.
transcript.zh: 不对，我记不清时间了，甚至可能是去年吧。总之就在过去一年半里，我去过一趟台北，见了一些立场非常进步、也非常支持“台独”的活动人士。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But they said, you know, we recognize that there is just no realistic path to Taiwanese independence right now. So what we think the best approach is to just kind of keep things chill, and maybe opportunities open up in the future.
transcript.zh: 但他们当时说，我们也认识到目前台湾独立并没有现实的路径可走，所以我们认为最好的做法就是暂时保持现状平和稳定，也许未来会出现新的契机。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But we just want to avoid a conflict; we want to continue to build our democracy here in Taiwan, to build our economy. And that makes sense to me.
transcript.zh: 他们说，我们只希望避免冲突，继续在台湾建设我们的民主、发展我们的经济。这番话在我看来非常合情合理。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: You know, so again, getting back to, you know, Samm, your question at the beginning of solidarity—I mean, solidarity with my colleagues in Taiwan who want to live, you know, a democratic life, you know, that approach makes sense to me.
transcript.zh: 所以回到 Samm 你一开始提到的“团结”这个问题——对我而言，声援那些希望过上民主生活的台湾同行，这种务实的做法是说得通的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So I want to be respectful of your time, Matt. I know you're terribly jet-lagged, and you just came back from Europe, I understand.
transcript.zh: Matt，我想体谅一下你的时间，我知道你刚从欧洲回来，倒时差一定非常辛苦。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And any incoherence in this interview I will blame on that, so just...
transcript.zh: 这次访谈里要是有任何语无伦次的地方，我就全推到时差头上，先说好……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, we'll just write off to that, but you've been very, very coherent. Samm, last question before we wrap up from you. What do you—anything...
transcript.zh: 好，那我们就全记在时差账上，不过你刚才的表达一直都非常清晰连贯。Samm，结束前最后一个问题交给你，你还有什么想……

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: I said earlier that I think the Democrats face a reckoning, and I think that that merits some unpacking because it may not be obvious what that reckoning is.
transcript.zh: 我前面提到过，我认为民主党正面临一场清算，我觉得这一点值得展开剖析，因为这场清算究竟意味着什么，或许并不一目了然。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: And I want to hone in on this idea that, you know, the AI race with China has long been used by tech oligarchs as the go-to argument against regulation.
transcript.zh: 我想聚焦这样一个现实：长期以来，科技寡头一直把“与中国的 AI 竞赛”当作反对监管的首选说辞。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: And coming out of the midterms, we have seen that the "but we will lose to China" will not fly with an American public that is concerned about job loss, about the sustainability of AI.
transcript.zh: 而在中期选举之后，我们已经看到，“不然我们就会输给中国”这套说辞，在担忧失业问题以及 AI 可持续性的美国公众面前已经行不通了。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: But the reason that I say the Democrats face a reckoning is because if we look at the Biden administration alums who are bent on China as an existential risk and a rival that needs to trump everything else,
transcript.zh: 但之所以说民主党面临一场清算，是因为看看那些曾效力于拜登政府的前官员们——他们执意将中国视为必须压倒一切其他议题的生存性风险与战略对手，

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: how do we reconcile that framing and that group of national security Democrats that wants to come back in in 2028 and resume power with the mandate from the American public to take on tech oligarchs, not just Nvidia, but Anthropic and others that are sounding the war drum with China?
transcript.zh: 这种叙事框架，以及那批想在 2028 年重返舞台、重新掌权的国家安全派民主党人，又该如何与美国公众的授权相调和？公众要求他们打击科技寡头——不仅是 Nvidia，还有 Anthropic 等正在擂响对华战鼓的企业。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: This is the reckoning I'm talking about. You have anti-war and you have anti-big-tech concentration of power colliding with "let's not regulate because China is the existential rival of our time."
transcript.zh: 这就是我所说的清算。反战诉求与反对大型科技公司权力集中的呼声，正与“因为中国是我们这个时代的生存性对手，所以不要监管”的论调正面相撞。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: How do you reconcile that? How will the Democrats reconcile that?
transcript.zh: 你要如何调和这种矛盾？民主党又将如何调和这种矛盾？

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Well, I think we need...
transcript.zh: 嗯，我认为我们需要……

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Democrats who are much better and going to be much more forceful in pointing the finger where it belongs when it comes to the challenges that American workers are facing.
transcript.zh: 我们需要更优秀、也更强硬的民主党人，在涉及美国工人面临的困境时，把矛头直指真正该负责任的对象。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And making the point that it wasn't China that deindustrialized the Rust Belt. It wasn't China that chose to ship jobs overseas. China was very happy to receive a lot of those jobs.
transcript.zh: 要明确指出，让“铁锈地带”去工业化的不是中国，选择把工作岗位转移到海外的也不是中国。中国固然乐于承接大量这样的岗位，

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: But these decisions that impoverished huge swaths of the American heartland, that was American corporations, aided by American politicians who had been bought off by those corporations and in turn gave those corporations tax incentives to move those jobs overseas.
transcript.zh: 但令美国腹地大片地区陷入贫困的那些决策，正是美国企业做出的——背后还有被这些企业收买、转而给予它们税收优惠以将岗位外迁的美国政客推波助澜。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So the idea that we're going to solve these problems by empowering these corporations and these even worse oligarchs is just daft.
transcript.zh: 因此，认为靠进一步赋能这些企业以及这些更糟糕的寡头就能解决问题，简直荒谬透顶。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So I think the way we're going to kind of suppress and beat the anti-China argument is by choosing the right enemy.
transcript.zh: 所以，我认为要压制并击败反华论调，关键在于选对敌人。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: The right enemy is corporate America. The right enemy is these oligarchs who have been working hand in hand with corrupt politicians.
transcript.zh: 真正的敌人是美国企业界，是这些与腐败政客狼狈为奸的寡头。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And again, this is populism about who are... I think we need to choose the right enemies. And this gets back to the concentration of power, issues of anti-corruption.
transcript.zh: 说到底，民粹主义的核心就在于划定敌我……我认为我们必须选对敌人。这又回到了权力集中与反腐败的问题上。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And I think focusing our ire in the right place—and again, it doesn't preclude having a serious conversation about the challenges that China does face—but I think we need to keep our focus here at home.
transcript.zh: 把愤怒的矛头对准真正的地方——当然，这并不妨碍我们就中国自身面临的挑战展开严肃讨论——但我认为我们必须把重心放在国内。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: The challenges we face most acutely are here at home by our own out-of-touch, self-dealing elite, and we will not solve those problems by empowering those elites.
transcript.zh: 我们面临的最紧迫的挑战就在国内，来自我们自己那些脱离民众、自肥谋私的精英阶层；继续向这些精英放权，绝无可能解决这些问题。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Matt Duss, executive vice president at the Center for International Policy and, more importantly, rocking guitar player like me. Well, thank you so much for joining us despite your jet lag.
transcript.zh: 以上是国际政策中心（Center for International Policy）执行副总裁Matt Duss——更重要的是，和我一样是个摇滚吉他手。非常感谢你顶着时差来参加我们的节目。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: We have a section of the show called Paying It Forward, where I ask my guests to name-check somebody who works with you or adjacent to you, a younger person who's coming up in the field and who deserves a little of our attention.
transcript.zh: 我们节目有一个叫“薪火相传”（Paying It Forward）的固定环节，请嘉宾推荐一位与你共事或邻近领域的年轻一代，他们正在业内崭露头角，值得大家多多关注。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Oh, man. Well, it's a surprise question, but here I'll just name a couple of people. One is my young friend—I think we mentioned him earlier in the podcast—Van Jackson.
transcript.zh: 哎呀，这问题挺突然的，不过我这就提几位吧。第一位是我的年轻朋友——我记得节目早些时候也提到过他——Van Jackson。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Really smart, really first-rate analyst.
transcript.zh: 他非常聪明，是真正一流的分析师。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Oh yeah, hardly needs our help.
transcript.zh: 哦是的，他几乎用不着我们帮衬。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Hardly needs my help, but I do want to acknowledge him and Mike Brenes again. They wrote a fantastic book, The Rivalry Peril, and they wrote the prologue for the book I edited.
transcript.zh: 的确不太需要我帮衬，但我还是想再次向他和Mike Brenes致意。他们合著了一本非常精彩的书《竞争的危险》（The Rivalry Peril），还为我主编的那本书撰写了序言。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Also want to mention my good friend Julia Gledhill, who is also a co-host with the podcast with Van and me and Julia called Un-Diplomatic. She is a fantastic defense analyst.
transcript.zh: 我还想提到我的好朋友Julia Gledhill，她也是我和Van一起主持的播客《非外交》（Un-Diplomatic）的联合主持人。她是一位非常优秀的防务分析师。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, she's whip-smart. So smart.
transcript.zh: 没错，她极其敏锐，太聪明了。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: She co-authored the chapter on cutting the defense budget in the book I edited, along with Bill Hartung. So those are just a couple names.
transcript.zh: 她还和Bill Hartung共同撰写了我主编那本书中关于削减国防预算的章节。这就是我想提到的两位。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Excellent. And next, on to Recommendations, where we talk about a movie or a TV show or a book—especially a book—something you've seen recently or something that you've read recently that you want to recommend to our readers.
transcript.zh: 太好了。接下来进入“推荐环节”（Recommendations），聊聊你最近看过的电影、剧集或读过的书——尤其是书——想推荐给我们听众的作品。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And we start with... let's start with Matt again.
transcript.zh: 我们从……还是先从Matt开始吧。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Oh man. Let's see...
transcript.zh: 天哪，让我想想……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: But Samm, you're on the hook for this too.
transcript.zh: 不过Samm，等会儿也少不了你的份。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I don't know if they're new, but it just popped up on my...
transcript.zh: 我不知道算不算新片，但刚才突然跳进我脑海里的是……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Don't need to be new.
transcript.zh: 不用非得是新的。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Doesn't need to be new, but I'm about to go watch it at some point, probably this week, for about the 20th time. It's Jodorowsky's Dune, if people have heard of this.
transcript.zh: 不用是新的就好。我大概这周某个时候又要去看大概第二十遍了，就是《佐杜洛夫斯基的沙丘》（Jodorowsky's Dune），不知道大家有没有听说过。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: I mean Dune, everyone I assume has seen the recent Dune movies with Timothée Chalamet. I think they're pretty good. However, Jodorowsky's Dune is a documentary about a version of Dune that was never made.
transcript.zh: 大家应该都看过Timothée Chalamet主演的近期《沙丘》（Dune）系列电影，我觉得拍得挺不错的。但《佐杜洛夫斯基的沙丘》是一部关于一版从未拍成的《沙丘》的纪录片。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Alejandro Jodorowsky, the experimental avant-garde filmmaker in the mid-to-late '70s, was planning to do a version of Dune. He brought together all these great artists, they storyboarded it, and it never got made.
transcript.zh: 实验先锋电影人Alejandro Jodorowsky在七十年代中后期曾计划执导一版《沙丘》。他集结了一众杰出的艺术家，画好了分镜脚本，但项目最终未能拍成。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: The financing fell through right before they were starting to shoot. But he did bring together some great artists who went on to do amazing work, including H.R. Giger and Dan O'Bannon, who went on to do Alien together.
transcript.zh: 就在准备开拍前夕，资金链断了。但他确实汇聚了一批后来成就斐然的艺术家，包括H.R. Giger和Dan O'Bannon——两人后来合作打造了《异形》（Alien）。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, Alien.
transcript.zh: 对，《异形》。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: So it's basically the most influential science fiction movie that never got made, but this documentary is just awesome.
transcript.zh: 所以它基本上称得上是影史上最具影响力、却从未拍成的科幻电影，而这部纪录片本身精彩绝伦。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: It's one of those things where I watched it on a flight somewhere and then watched it on the flight back, and I've watched it multiple times since then. It's great.
transcript.zh: 我就属于那种去程航班上看了一遍、返程航班上又看一遍的人，之后还重温过很多次。非常棒。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: The second thing I'll recommend is this Swedish stoner rock band called Slomosa that I just discovered—Slomosa, S-L-O-M-O-S-A.
transcript.zh: 我推荐的第二样东西是我刚发现的一支瑞典迷幻重摇滚（stoner rock）乐队，叫Slomosa——拼写是S-L-O-M-O-S-A。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: And it's just one of those records that has really, really grabbed me, and I can't stop listening to it. So going to recommend Slomosa.
transcript.zh: 他们的专辑就是那种一下就把我彻底抓住的唱片，我听得完全停不下来。所以我要推荐Slomosa。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: All right, I'll check it out. I'll check it out.
transcript.zh: 好，我去听听看，一定去听听。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: All right, Samm, you're up. What do you got?
transcript.zh: 好了，Samm，轮到你了。你有什么推荐？

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: So since we were in Beijing talking about this on the last podcast we did together in July, I'm still on my non-fiction kick and narrative non-fiction. I'm reading The Frenchmen, My Life in—or On My Life and Theory, by Emily Eakin.
transcript.zh: 自从7月我们在北京一起录上一期播客聊到这个话题以来，我至今还沉浸在非虚构和叙事非虚构作品里。我最近在读Emily Eakin的《The Frenchmen》，副标题是“My Life in”——不对，是“On My Life and Theory”。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: And it's about sort of murder and madness and gossip, looking at all the French postmodern theorists.
transcript.zh: 这本书大致围绕谋杀、癫狂与八卦展开，审视了那批法国后现代主义理论家。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: But it's told from this perspective of the author who decided, you know, when she was in college, she wanted to study the structuralists because she thought they were cool, and she wanted, you know, men to woo her in her college dorm who were also studying the French postmodern theorists.
transcript.zh: 不过它是从作者本人的视角来写的——她上大学时觉得结构主义学者很酷，于是决定专攻这方面，而且也希望宿舍里那些同样研究法国后现代理论的男生来追求自己。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: But what I love about this book, and I think is relevant now, is she's not just like diving deep in their theory, which none of us can really understand, but it sort of steps back.
transcript.zh: 但我喜欢这本书的地方——而且我觉得放在当下也很有现实意义——在于她并没有一味深究那些我们谁也真正读不懂的理论，而是退后一步来观察。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: And it talks about, how do we make meaning in an unstable world when we're reading texts and media and it's all mediated? So like, what does Instagram and ChatGPT mean?
transcript.zh: 她探讨的是：当我们在一个不稳定的世界里阅读文本与媒体、而一切信息又都经过媒介过滤时，我们该如何建构意义？比如，Instagram和ChatGPT又意味着什么？

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: And also, what about journalism in China in an era where there are increasingly less journalists in China, and we have all of these narratives about what China means for US domestic agendas?
transcript.zh: 此外，在一个中国驻地记者越来越少的时代，中国的新闻报道又该如何看待？与此同时，外界充斥着各种关于中国对美国国内议程意味着什么的叙事。

transcript.speaker: Samm Sacks
transcript.en: But it's just a fun read, and I love reading really good narrative non-fiction. So I recommend that.
transcript.zh: 总之这本书读起来非常有趣，我特别喜欢优秀的叙事非虚构作品，所以推荐给大家。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Oh, sounds terrific. I'll definitely pick it up.
transcript.zh: 听起来太棒了，我一定会找来读读。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So for my recommendation, I'm rereading Benedict Anderson's Imagined Communities ahead of a couple conversations I know I'm going to be in, conversations that involve, you know, nationalism and state formation and ideas about civilization and things of that nature.
transcript.zh: 至于我的推荐，我正在重读Benedict Anderson的《想象的共同体》（Imagined Communities），为接下来要参与的几场对谈做准备——这些对谈会涉及民族主义、国家建构以及文明观念之类的话题。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's actually been a really long time, and I'm surprised at how well it reads and how insightful it still remains. It's really good. I do recommend it.
transcript.zh: 其实我离上次读已经过去很久了，很惊讶它至今读来依然流畅，洞见也依然犀利。真的非常出色，我强烈推荐。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I'm going to have to try to force myself next to read Samuel Huntington's Clash of Civilizations, that much-maligned book, because I've been, you know, talking about his ideas without actually having read the thing, which is something I feel kind of guilty about.
transcript.zh: 接下来我得逼自己去读一读Samuel Huntington那本备受诟病的《文明的冲突》（Clash of Civilizations），因为我一直都在谈论他的观点，却其实没真正读过原书，对此我多少有点惭愧。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I'm sure I am not going to come out of it a convert or anything, but with the whole civilizationalism project taking root in America, in Russia, in India, maybe even in China, I feel like I should brush up on the vocab and some of the main concepts.
transcript.zh: 我肯定不会读完就变成他的信徒，但眼下整套“文明论”工程正在美国、俄罗斯、印度乃至中国生根发芽，我觉得还是有必要重温一下相关术语和核心概念。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So that's what I'm rereading right now.
transcript.zh: 这就是我眼下正在重读的书。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Once again, thank you so much. Samm, thanks. It was great to have you join as co-host. Matt, thank you so much for making the time. It's a terrific conversation, and I look forward to more of them.
transcript.zh: 再次非常感谢两位。谢谢Samm，很高兴请你来担任联合主持。Matt，非常感谢你抽出时间。这场对话非常精彩，期待以后还有更多交流。

transcript.speaker: Matt Duss
transcript.en: Thanks. Really glad to be with you both.
transcript.zh: 谢谢，很高兴能和你们二位一起录制。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You've been listening to the Sinica Podcast. The show is produced, recorded, engineered, edited, and mastered by me, Kaiser Kuo.
transcript.zh: 感谢收听《Sinica Podcast》。本期节目由我——Kaiser Kuo——负责制作、录制、音频工程、剪辑及母带处理。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Don't forget to leave a review on Apple Podcasts or wherever you listen. Huge thanks to my guest, Matt Duss, and of course, my lovely co-host, Samm Sacks. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you next week. Take care.
transcript.zh: 别忘了在Apple Podcasts或你常用的收听平台留下评价。衷心感谢本期嘉宾Matt Duss，当然还有我可爱的联合主持人Samm Sacks。感谢收听，我们下周再见，保重！
